meta.title: Supplement Evidence Audit
meta.subtitle: 121 consumer-supplement compounds graded 1-5 on independent human-trial evidence, organized by outcome
meta.method: 67-agent adversarial research workflow. One skeptical researcher per category re-derived every grade from primary trials (7 existing categories challenged against a prior summary-depth pass; 5 new categories graded from scratch), applying seven mandatory bias checks: funding-source subgroup, outlier leverage, effect-size vs MCID, trial dose vs retail dose, population transfer, dose-response direction, and regulatory advisories. 50 high-stakes/compromised/moved grades were then handed to an independent adversarial reviewer instructed to REFUTE them. 703 tool calls, ~2.6M tokens.

scoring.5: Large independent RCTs, consistent, clinically meaningful. Would bet on it.
scoring.4: Multiple good RCTs, real but modest, or narrower population than marketed.
scoring.3: Real signal, but small/short trials or needs specific conditions to appear.
scoring.2: Positive results concentrated in industry-funded or low-quality studies. Mechanism outruns outcome.
scoring.1: Marketing. No credible human outcome data.

meta.key_caveat: Grades reflect EVIDENCE QUALITY, not whether a compound 'works' for you. 88 grades are conditional on a personal value (a deficiency, a specific complaint, a dose). Product links are Amazon SEARCH URLs (not fixed product pages) chosen for ingredient form and dose; verify the per-serving ACTIVE dose before buying. Not medical advice.

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Check 3 (effect size vs MCID) — the only real point of attack — held; the confirming pillars were Check 4 (dose match) and Check 5 (population transfer)
compounds.trial_count: 16 RCTs (2024 meta) plus acute MRS trial
compounds.total_n: ~492 across 16 RCTs (Prokopidis Frontiers Nutr 2024 meta); acute sleep-dep trial n=15
compounds.largest_independent_trial: No single large independent healthy-adult cognition RCT; evidence rests on the pooled 16-trial meta (Prokopidis, Frontiers in Nutrition 2024) and the n=15 MRS sleep-dep trial.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Memory SMD ~0.3 (GRADE moderate) in 2024 meta; processing-speed/attention low certainty. Acute trial: improved PVT and processing speed during 21 h sleep deprivation, effect from ~3.5 h, peak ~4 h.
compounds.clears_mcid: Borderline. Meaningful under metabolic stress (sleep loss, vegetarian repletion); marginal in rested omnivores.
compounds.trial_dose: Chronic cognition trials 5-20 g/day; acute sleep-deprivation protocol 0.35 g/kg single dose
compounds.retail_dose: 3-5 g/day creatine monohydrate (fully active, no elemental discount)
compounds.population_studied: Mixed: healthy young adults, vegetarians, older adults, and sleep-deprived young men. Largest cognitive effects in metabolically stressed or creatine-depleted subgroups.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Partial. Benefit largest when muscle/brain creatine is low; rested well-fed omnivore gains little.
compounds.funding_split: Not cleanly reported in the 2024 meta; effect not obviously funding-dependent.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Small total n is the main fragility; not driven by one extreme study.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: EFSA 2024 evaluated a creatine + cognitive-function health claim (Article 13(5)); not established/authorized. No safety advisory, strong safety record.
compounds.movement_note: Dropped 5 to 4. The '16-RCT meta, GRADE moderate' is real but the pooled base is only ~492 subjects, memory SMD is modest, and the largest effects concentrate in creatine-DEPLETED states (vegetarians, older adults, sleep deprivation). The 2024 sleep-deprivation result (Gordji-Nejad, Sci Rep 2024) used a single 0.35 g/kg dose (~25 g for a 70 kg adult, n=15), not the 3-5 g/day retail regimen. As a memory supplement for a healthy, rested, omnivorous adult it is a 4, not a 'would bet on it' 5.
compounds.conditional_on: Clearest benefit conditional on creatine depletion: vegetarian/vegan diet, age, or acute sleep deprivation. Acute cognitive rescue needs ~0.35 g/kg, far above the 3-5 g/day maintenance dose.
compounds.verdict: The best-evidenced item in this category, but the prior grade of 5 overstates it for the marketed use. Worth buying if you are vegetarian, older, or acutely sleep-deprived; the general healthy-rested-adult memory benefit is small. Cheap, safe, well-characterized.
primary_sources: Prokopidis K, et al. Frontiers in Nutrition 2024;11:1424972 (16-RCT meta, PMC11275561)
Gordji-Nejad A, et al. Scientific Reports 2024;14:4937, doi:10.1038/s41598-024-54249-9
Xu C, et al. Nutrients 2026;18:1192 (single-dose creatine, sleep deprivation)
EFSA Journal 2024;22:e9100 (creatine + cognition health-claim evaluation)

products.dose_per_serving_active: 5 g creatine monohydrate per scoop (fully active; no elemental discount)
products.servings_per_day_to_hit_trial_dose: 1 scoop/day for standard 5 g cognition dosing; 1-4 scoops for the 5-20 g/day chronic range; the acute 0.35 g/kg sleep-deprivation dose (~25 g for a 70 kg adult) would need ~5 scoops as a one-off
products.note: Best-in-class pick: uses Creapure (the branded form used in most cognition/creatine trials) and is NSF Certified for Sport. 5 g/scoop meets the standard chronic cognition dose. Unflavored powder. ASIN varies by listing; search URL is reliable.

products.dose_per_serving_active: 5 g creatine monohydrate per scoop
products.servings_per_day_to_hit_trial_dose: 1 scoop/day for maintenance; 2-4 scoops/day (10-20 g) for higher cognition/sleep-deprivation dosing
products.note: Best-in-class pick: branded Creapure creatine monohydrate AND NSF Certified for Sport (strongest anti-adulteration mark). 5 g/scoop fully covers the 3-5 g maintenance/muscle-energy dose and the low end of cognition dosing; sits at the LOW end of the 5-20 g cognition range and below the ~14-18 g single-dose sleep-deprivation protocol (would need 3-4 scoops). Alternative also NSF: Klean Athlete Klean Creatine (also Creapure).

compounds.trial_count: Multiple large RCTs (VITAL) + phase IIa DHA target-engagement trial
compounds.total_n: VITAL cognitive n=4218; USC DHA trial small phase IIa; multiple prior meta-analyses
compounds.largest_independent_trial: VITAL (Kang JH et al., Alz Dement TRCI 2022;8:e12288), n=4218, marine n-3 1 g/day, NO cognitive benefit over 2-3 yr.
compounds.effect_size_ci: VITAL: no significant difference in global cognition change vs placebo (null). USC: biomarker positive (CSF DHA +17%), cognition null.
compounds.clears_mcid: No, primary cognitive endpoints did not differ from placebo in the large trials.
compounds.trial_dose: VITAL 1 g/day fish oil (840 mg EPA+DHA); USC 2 g/day DHA
compounds.retail_dose: ~200-400 mg DHA per softgel (algal DHA ~400-500 mg); many '1000 mg fish oil' caps deliver far less DHA
compounds.population_studied: Generally healthy older adults (VITAL) and older adults at dementia risk with low dietary DHA (<200 mg/day) and >=1 risk factor (USC trial).
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No. Replete healthy adults show no benefit; signal is deficiency-repletion, not enhancement.
compounds.funding_split: VITAL and USC are NIH/independent, and they are the null trials, which strengthens the negative read.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Older positive meta-signals lean on small trials in low-DHA or MCI populations; large trials wash them out.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Dose-response safety signal (check #6): prescription 4 g/day EPA (REDUCE-IT) and STRENGTH raised atrial-fibrillation risk; high-dose omega-3 is not benign. No memory-specific advisory.
compounds.movement_note: Nudged 3.5 to 3 (half point, not flagged). Decisive new evidence is negative: VITAL (n=4218) showed no cognitive benefit over 2-3 yr, and the 2024/2026 USC high-dose DHA trial (2 g/day, 24 mo, at-risk older adults) confirmed CSF DHA penetrance (+17% at 6 mo) but NULL cognition. Large independent trials are null; benefit confined to low-status/APOE4 subgroups.
compounds.conditional_on: Any cognitive rationale is conditional on a low omega-3 index / low dietary DHA and possibly APOE e4 status; not for replete adults.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for memory as a healthy, omega-3-replete adult. The large independent trials are null. A conditional signal survives only in people with low omega-3 status or genetic/early-neurodegeneration risk. Prior of 3.5 slightly generous.
primary_sources: Kang JH, et al. Alzheimers Dement (N Y) TRCI 2022;8:e12288 (VITAL cognition, null)
USC high-dose DHA trial, eBioMedicine 2026, PIIS2352-3964(26)00198-2
REDUCE-IT (Bhatt DL, NEJM 2019) / STRENGTH (Nicholls SJ, JAMA 2020) atrial-fibrillation signal

products.note: Vegan/algal alternative and the higher-DHA-fraction choice, but flagged dose_adequate=false against the 2 g DHA trial target — it takes many softgels/day. Good match if the goal is the 200-400 mg DHA maintenance range.

compounds.verify_decisive_check: funding-source
compounds.trial_count: 2 small RCTs in healthy older adults (discordant), plus stroke/dementia trials
compounds.total_n: Nakazaki 2022 n=100; second (1 g) RCT similar size; small overall for the healthy-adult claim
compounds.largest_independent_trial: No large independent healthy-adult trial; stroke trials (ICTUS, Davalos 2012, n=2298) were NEUTRAL for a different indication.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Nakazaki 2022: significant improvement in composite/episodic memory vs placebo at 12 wk (industry-funded); not replicated at 1 g/day.
compounds.clears_mcid: Uncertain, small trial, no established MCID; effect not robust across doses.
compounds.trial_dose: 500 mg/day (Nakazaki, positive) vs 1 g/day (non-replication)
compounds.retail_dose: Cognizin 250-500 mg/day (250 mg products fall below the 500 mg trial dose)
compounds.population_studied: Healthy older adults (55-91 yr) with age-associated memory impairment (AAMI); also stroke/vascular-cognitive populations (different indication).
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Weak. Signal is in AAMI older adults; no convincing effect in younger healthy adults.
compounds.funding_split: The positive healthy-adult RCT is manufacturer-funded (Kyowa Hakko Bio / Cognizin); independent replication absent.
compounds.outlier_leverage: The healthy-adult case rests essentially on one manufacturer-funded trial.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: EFSA Journal 2024;22:e8861, no cause-effect relationship established between citicoline and memory. (Prescription drug in some EU/Asian markets, not US.)
compounds.movement_note: Down 3 to 2.5. The key positive healthy-adult trial (Nakazaki 2022) is funded by Kyowa Hakko Bio, the maker of Cognizin citicoline, and a second RCT at 1 g/day did NOT replicate the episodic-memory effect. EFSA 2024 concluded no cause-effect relationship for memory. Funding-source and non-replication flags apply.
compounds.conditional_on: Any signal is conditional on age-associated memory impairment and the 500 mg dose; does not extend to healthy younger adults.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy on current evidence. The one supportive healthy-adult RCT is industry-funded and was not replicated at higher dose, and EFSA (2024) rejected the memory health claim. Prior of 3 is slightly optimistic.
primary_sources: Nakazaki E, et al. J Nutr 2022;152:2415-2425, doi:10.1016/j.tjnut.2022.06.001 (Cognizin, manufacturer-funded)
EFSA Journal 2024;22:e8861 (citicoline + memory health claim, negative)
Davalos A, et al. (ICTUS) Lancet 2012;380:349-357 (citicoline in stroke, neutral)

compounds.trial_count: 9 RCTs (2014 meta); several 12-wk 300 mg trials since
compounds.largest_independent_trial: No single large independent trial; Stough 2001/2008 (CDRI-08, ~n=46-107) and Calabrese 2008 (n=54, 300 mg, 12 wk) are the anchors.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Meta: significant improvement in Trail-Making/choice-RT and speed of attention; decreased reaction time. Memory (free recall) improvements less consistent.
compounds.clears_mcid: Modest; attention/RT changes small-to-moderate, no formal MCID.
compounds.trial_dose: 300-450 mg/day standardized extract (~55% bacosides, or Bacognize/CDRI-08)
compounds.retail_dose: 300-320 mg standardized extract (matches trials), but many non-standardized 'Bacopa 500 mg' whole-herb products deliver far less bacoside
compounds.population_studied: Healthy adults, medical students, and older adults with age-associated memory impairment; 300 mg standardized extract, 12 wk.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Partial, some healthy-adult and student trials positive, but onset requires chronic (>=8-12 wk) dosing.
compounds.funding_split: No clean funding-split meta; several trials use proprietary extracts (CDRI-08, Bacognize) with sponsor involvement.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Small trials; heterogeneous extracts limit pooling confidence.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No major regulator efficacy authorization; commonly reported GI adverse effects (nausea, cramping, diarrhea, increased stool frequency).
compounds.movement_note: Held at 3. Kongkeaw 2014 meta (9 RCTs, 437 subjects) shows improved speed of attention and reduced choice reaction time; memory-consolidation effects are weaker and slow to appear. Trials small and short; effect real but narrow.
compounds.conditional_on: Benefit conditional on a standardized bacoside extract and >=12 weeks of use; whole-herb/underdosed products unlikely to work.
compounds.verdict: Conditional buy at best. Real but modest signal, mainly on speed of attention / reaction time rather than memory, and it takes ~12 weeks. Use a standardized extract (55% bacosides / Bacognize) at 300 mg. GI side effects common. Prior of 3 holds.
primary_sources: Kongkeaw C, et al. J Ethnopharmacol 2014;151:528-535 (9-RCT meta)
Calabrese C, et al. J Altern Complement Med 2008;14:707-713 (300 mg, 12 wk, healthy elderly)
Stough C, et al. Psychopharmacology 2001;156:481-484 (CDRI-08)

products.form: Bacopa monnieri extract standardized to 45% bacosides (generic high-potency extract, not a branded clinical form)
products.dose_per_serving_active: ~450 mg bacosides per 1000 mg extract serving (at 45% standardization)
products.servings_per_day_to_hit_trial_dose: 1 serving/day delivers bacoside content at/above the 300-450 mg standardized-extract trials (which use ~12-55% bacosides). Could split to a smaller dose and remain within trial range
products.note: Chosen because bacoside content is explicitly standardized and high, avoiding the common 'Bacopa 500 mg' whole-herb trap that delivers little bacoside. However it is NOT a trial-branded form. Preferred if available: Bacognize or Synapsa (CDRI-08/KeenMind) — search 'Bacognize Bacopa' or 'Synapsa Bacopa' on Amazon; those are the exact clinically-studied extracts but stock/listings are intermittent.

compounds.trial_count: Multiple large RCTs + Cochrane review (Birks/Wieland)
compounds.total_n: GEM n=3069; GuidAge n=2854; Cochrane pooled thousands
compounds.largest_independent_trial: GEM Study (DeKosky ST, JAMA 2008;300:2253-2262), n=3069, EGb761 240 mg/day, NULL for dementia prevention.
compounds.effect_size_ci: GEM: no reduction in dementia incidence (HR ~1.12, 95% CI 0.94-1.33, no benefit). Cochrane: little-to-no effect on global clinical status at 6 mo (moderate certainty).
compounds.clears_mcid: No, prevention trials null; treatment effects inconsistent and below reliable clinical significance.
compounds.trial_dose: EGb761 120-240 mg/day (prevention trials used 240 mg)
compounds.retail_dose: Commonly 120 mg/day standardized extract (below the 240 mg used in the treatment trials that occasionally signal)
compounds.population_studied: Older adults (GEM, GuidAge prevention); dementia/cognitive-impairment patients (treatment trials). Little healthy-young-adult data.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No. No credible benefit in cognitively healthy adults.
compounds.funding_split: The one recent outlier trial reporting 'very large' effects contrasts with three concurrent null trials; positive results cluster in manufacturer-linked/lower-quality studies.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Cochrane explicitly notes one trial with large effects against a backdrop of nulls, classic outlier leverage.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Bleeding-risk / anticoagulant-antiplatelet interaction widely flagged (perioperative bleeding, potentiation of warfarin/aspirin). No efficacy authorization.
compounds.movement_note: Held at 2. The two large independent prevention RCTs, GEM (DeKosky, JAMA 2008, n=3069) and GuidAge (Vellas, Lancet Neurol 2012, n=2854), were NULL for preventing dementia. Cochrane: evidence inconsistent and unreliable. No convincing healthy-adult memory benefit.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for memory. Large independent prevention trials are null and Cochrane calls the dementia evidence inconsistent and unreliable. Carries a real bleeding/anticoagulant interaction. Prior of 2 holds.
primary_sources: DeKosky ST, et al. (GEM) JAMA 2008;300:2253-2262
Vellas B, et al. (GuidAge) Lancet Neurol 2012;11:851-859
Birks J / Wieland LS, Cochrane Database Syst Rev (CD003120; CD013661)

compounds.trial_count: Small AD add-on RCTs (ASCOMALVA) + large safety cohort
compounds.total_n: ASCOMALVA n~210; Korean safety cohort >12 million
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Largest dataset is a SAFETY study: Lee G, et al. (Korean NHIS cohort) 2021, >12M subjects, dose-dependent higher 10-yr stroke incidence in alpha-GPC users.
compounds.effect_size_ci: ASCOMALVA: modest cognitive/behavioral benefit as add-on to donepezil in AD (small, industry-associated). No healthy-adult effect size available.
compounds.clears_mcid: Not established in any non-dementia population.
compounds.trial_dose: 1200 mg/day (400 mg three times daily) in AD trials
compounds.retail_dose: 300-600 mg/day (below the 1200 mg trial dose)
compounds.population_studied: Alzheimer's and vascular-cognitive-impairment patients (efficacy trials). No healthy-adult cognitive-enhancement evidence.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No. Trials are in dementia; no memory-enhancement data in healthy adults.
compounds.funding_split: Positive efficacy concentrated in a single manufacturer-associated AD trial program.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Efficacy case leans on the ASCOMALVA program; safety signal is the more robust, larger dataset.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Stroke-risk safety signal in the Korean nationwide cohort (proposed via choline to TMAO). No efficacy authorization.
compounds.movement_note: Held at 2. Benefit evidence is the ASCOMALVA add-on-to-donepezil AD trials (not healthy adults). Decisive downgrade pressure comes from safety: a >12-million-person Korean cohort (Lee et al. 2021) found a dose-dependent ~46% higher 10-year stroke risk in users.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy. Efficacy data are confined to add-on dementia trials (mostly industry/AD, not healthy adults), and a large cohort shows a dose-dependent 10-year stroke-risk signal. Risk outruns any consumer benefit; the safety signal makes this a firm avoid.
primary_sources: Lee G, et al. Association of L-alpha-GPC with subsequent stroke risk (Korean NHIS cohort, >12M), 2021
Amenta F, et al. (ASCOMALVA) J Neurol Sci / J Alzheimers Dis 2012-2014 (add-on to donepezil in AD)

compounds.verify_decisive_check: population transfer
compounds.trial_count: Several small RCTs; strongest (bovine) is the wrong molecule for retail
compounds.total_n: Bovine PS: Cenacchi n=494 (not the retail form); soy-PS trials n=30-120 each
compounds.largest_independent_trial: No large independent soy-PS trial; Cenacchi 1993 (bovine, n=494) is the largest but is the wrong molecule.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Vakhapova 2010 (soy-PS 300 mg): improvement in a memory subgroup with low baseline; several endpoints not significant vs placebo. Mixed.
compounds.clears_mcid: Not reliably; soy-PS effects small and inconsistent.
compounds.trial_dose: 300-600 mg/day; historical bovine trials 300 mg/day
compounds.retail_dose: 100-300 mg/day soy-derived PS (often 100 mg, below trial dose and wrong source)
compounds.population_studied: Older adults with age-associated memory impairment or subjective memory complaints. Bovine-PS trials in the elderly; soy-PS trials smaller.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No. Signal is in impaired older adults, not healthy adults; and the strongest data are from a discontinued bovine product.
compounds.funding_split: Soy-PS trials often industry-supported (Enzymotec/Lipogen); independent replication thin.
compounds.outlier_leverage: The category's reputation rests on the old bovine-PS trial that is not the retail substance.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: FDA permits only a QUALIFIED health claim for PS with a disclaimer that the evidence is 'very limited and preliminary.' No authorized memory claim.
compounds.movement_note: Held at 2. Critical population/source mismatch (check #5): the historically positive trial (Cenacchi 1993, n=494) used BOVINE-cortex PS, no longer sold due to BSE/prion concern. Retail soy-PS trials (Vakhapova, Richter) are smaller and inconsistent, with one showing placebo-equal gains. is_compromised=true because the supportive evidence does not transfer to the product on shelves.
compounds.conditional_on: Any weak signal is conditional on age-associated memory impairment; does not apply to healthy adults.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy the retail (soy) product for memory. The good early data used bovine-cortex PS (withdrawn over prion risk); the soy PS that is actually sold has weak, mixed trials, and FDA allows only a heavily-qualified claim. Prior of 2 holds.
primary_sources: Cenacchi T, et al. Aging Clin Exp Res 1993;5:123-133 (bovine-cortex PS, n=494)
Vakhapova V, et al. Dement Geriatr Cogn Disord 2010;29:467-474 (soy-PS 300 mg)
FDA qualified health claim letter for phosphatidylserine (2003)

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Population transfer (disease AChE-deficit patients vs healthy adults), reinforced by the negative independent Western trial
compounds.trial_count: 20 RCTs (all China, high risk of bias)
compounds.largest_independent_trial: No rigorous Western independent trial; a US NIH-funded phase II (Rafii 2011, n=210) was essentially NEGATIVE at 200 mcg twice daily.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Yang 2013: significant MMSE and ADL improvement vs placebo in AD at 8-16 wk; effect grew with duration, but pooled from high-bias trials.
compounds.clears_mcid: Reported MMSE gains in AD may reach clinical relevance, but bias undermines the estimate; irrelevant to healthy adults.
compounds.trial_dose: 300-500 mcg/day for 8-24 weeks
compounds.retail_dose: 50-200 mcg/day (typically below the 300-500 mcg trial dose)
compounds.population_studied: Alzheimer's disease and vascular dementia patients in China. No healthy-adult cognitive-enhancement RCTs.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No. AChE inhibition in AD is not memory enhancement in healthy adults; cholinergic side effects expected.
compounds.funding_split: Not formally split; the entire evidence base is a single-country, high-risk-of-bias cluster.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Whole meta is low-quality; effect could shrink substantially under rigorous trials.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Sold as a supplement in the US but pharmacologically a reversible AChE inhibitor (prescription drug class elsewhere); cholinergic adverse effects. No efficacy authorization.
compounds.movement_note: Held at 1.5. Yang 2013 (PLoS ONE, 20 RCTs, n=1823) shows MMSE improvement in AD, but ALL trials are Chinese with high risk of bias, a classic low-quality cluster and non-generalizable. is_compromised=true: the positive signal depends on biased, single-country trials. It is a drug-like AChE inhibitor, not a benign nootropic.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy as a consumer memory supplement. It is a genuine acetylcholinesterase inhibitor (same pharmacology as donepezil) sold unregulated; the AD efficacy meta-analyses are entirely China-based with high risk of bias, and there is no healthy-adult benefit data. Prior of 1.5 holds.
primary_sources: Yang G, et al. PLoS ONE 2013;8:e74916 (20-RCT meta, all China)
Rafii MS, et al. Neurology 2011;76:1389-1394 (US phase II, negative)
Xing SH, et al. Evid Based Complement Alternat Med 2014;2014:363985

compounds.trial_count: Multiple small metabolic RCTs; ~1 exploratory cognition trial
compounds.total_n: Meta-analyses pool small metabolic RCTs; Wu 2025 NR trial small
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Wu Y, et al. Alzheimers Dement (N Y) TRCI 2025;11:e70023 (NR in SCD/MCI): biomarker shifts, no clear cognitive benefit.
compounds.effect_size_ci: NAD+ significantly elevated; clinically relevant metabolic/cognitive outcomes not significantly different from control.
compounds.clears_mcid: No cognitive outcome measured that could clear any MCID.
compounds.trial_dose: NMN 250-1000 mg/day; NR 250-1000 mg/day
compounds.retail_dose: NMN 250-500 mg/day; NR ~300 mg/day (doses match trials, but no efficacy endpoint to underdose against)
compounds.population_studied: Mostly metabolic-health cohorts; one 2025 NR trial in subjective cognitive decline / MCI. No healthy-adult memory outcome trials.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No, no human memory benefit demonstrated in any population.
compounds.funding_split: Small trials often industry-linked; irrelevant because outcomes are null regardless.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not applicable, no positive cognitive outcome to leverage.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: FDA (2022) took the position that NMN is excluded from the dietary-supplement definition because it is under investigation as a drug (MIB-626), unresolved US legal status.
compounds.movement_note: Held at 1.5. Meta-analyses confirm NMN robustly raises NAD+ but shows no significant clinically-relevant outcome vs control. The 2025 NR trial in SCD/MCI (Wu et al., Alz Dement TRCI) moved biomarkers with minimal/null cognitive change. Mechanism-only; human memory outcomes absent.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for memory. These reliably raise blood NAD+ but have no downstream cognitive outcome in humans; the biology outruns the evidence. NMN also has an unresolved US regulatory status. Prior of 1.5 holds.
primary_sources: Wu Y, et al. Alzheimers Dement (N Y) 2025;11:e70023 (NR, SCD/MCI)
NMN meta-analysis, Crit Rev Food Sci Nutr 2024, doi:10.1080/10408398.2024.2387324 (NAD+ up, outcomes null)
FDA position on NMN as excluded from supplement definition (2022)

compounds.trial_count: A few small RCTs; no large trial
compounds.total_n: Mori n=30; Docherty n=41; acute crossover n=18
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Docherty S, et al. (Frontiers in Nutrition / Nutrients 2023-2025), n=41 healthy adults, 1.8 g/28 d: acute Stroop speed only, no durable memory benefit.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Mori: cognitive-scale (HDS-R) rise during dosing that reversed after washout, small n. Docherty: significant Stroop speed at 60 min only; memory endpoints null; earlier healthy-adult study reported reduced delayed word recall.
compounds.clears_mcid: No, acute attention change is minor; no durable memory benefit clearing an MCID.
compounds.trial_dose: Mori 3 g/day powder (16 wk); Docherty 1.8 g/day (28 d); acute 3 g 10:1 extract
compounds.retail_dose: 500-1000 mg/day, frequently non-standardized 10:1 extracts of unverified hericenone/erinacine content (typically below the 3 g whole-powder trial dose)
compounds.population_studied: Japanese older adults with MCI (Mori 2009); healthy young adults 18-45 (Docherty 2023). Mixed and small.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Poor. Benefit is limited to MCI; in healthy adults effects are acute/attentional at best and possibly negative for delayed recall.
compounds.funding_split: Mori trial industry-linked; independent healthy-adult trials are the more skeptical ones.
compounds.outlier_leverage: The reputation rests largely on the single small Mori MCI trial.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No efficacy authorization; generally regarded as safe (occasional dermatologic/GI reactions). No memory claim approved.
compounds.movement_note: Held at 2. compounds.total_n: ~127 in the key attention trial; hundreds across chronic/dementia pooling
compounds.largest_independent_trial: No sizable INDEPENDENT acute-focus trial; the dementia meta-analyses (independent) show only modest, heterogeneous benefit in impaired patients.

compounds.clears_mcid: Cannot confirm - effect sizes not transparently reported; no MCID established for the attention endpoints.

compounds.retail_dose: 250-500 mg (often as Cognizin) - matches trial dose, so dose is not the failure point; the problem is no acute data and industry-concentrated chronic data.
compounds.population_studied: Adults 35-75 with poor sustained attention (Nakazaki 2021); adolescent males (McGlade); MCI/dementia patients (meta-analyses). Not healthy rested adults acutely.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No - benefit, where seen, is in poor-attention or impaired populations over weeks; it does not transfer to acute focus in a healthy adult.
compounds.funding_split: Positive attention trials are Kyowa Hakko / Cognizin (Kirin) funded; no independent pooled-vs-industry split favors it. Independent large acute data absent.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not applicable in the classic sense, but the acute-focus case rests entirely on chronic industry trials.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No major Western regulator efficacy advisory; sold as a drug (Somazina/Ceraxon) in some countries, supplement in the US.
compounds.movement_note: Moved 3 -> 2. The prior score reflected general cognition. Re-read against the ACUTE-focus rubric: the two headline trials (Nakazaki 2021, n=127, 500 mg for 12 weeks in 35-75 yr olds with poor attention; McGlade adolescent-male attention study) are chronic, industry-funded (Kyowa Hakko/Cognizin), and in below-average-attention populations. No acute single-dose focus RCT in healthy adults exists. Dementia/MCI meta-analyses (Nutrients 2023, 15(2):386) show only a modest, heterogeneous signal in impaired populations.
compounds.conditional_on: Any benefit is conditional on 6-12 weeks of daily use in a poor-attention or cognitively-impaired population - not acute focus.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for ACUTE focus. There is essentially no single-dose acute-attention evidence; the supporting human trials are 12-week chronic supplementation, mostly industry-funded (Cognizin/Kyowa) and run in low-attention or clinical populations. compounds.clears_mcid: Cannot assess - no consistent outcome metric, no MCID benchmarking possible.
compounds.trial_dose: Commonly 200-576 mg/day of standardized extract (e.g. SHR-5, ~3% rosavins / 1% salidroside).
compounds.retail_dose: 200-500 mg standardized extract - broadly matches trial doses, so dose is not the limiting issue; evidence quality is.

compounds.funding_split: Positive fatigue findings concentrate in SHR-5 (Swedish Herbal Institute) manufacturer-linked trials; independent replication is sparse and inconsistent.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not formally poolable, but the fatigue signal leans on a small cluster of manufacturer trials.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No major hepatotoxicity or safety advisory found; EMA lists it as a traditional-use herbal (well-tolerated). One isolated case report of herb-herb interaction liver injury.
compounds.not_a_supplement: For fatigue-driven poor focus the durable fixes are sleep sufficiency and load management, not an adaptogen.
compounds.conditional_on: Any plausible benefit is conditional on a mental-fatigue/burnout state, not baseline focus.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for acute baseline focus. Signals exist for mental FATIGUE and burnout, not for sharpening a rested healthy adult. compounds.effect_size_ci: Military Medicine REA (10 RCTs + 4 non-RCTs) made only a WEAK recommendation; all showed directionally positive stress-mitigation but effect sizes/CIs are inconsistent and small-sample. No robust pooled CI exists.
compounds.clears_mcid: Unclear - benefits are context-specific (preventing decline under stress) rather than boosting baseline; no MCID framework applied.
compounds.trial_dose: 100-150 mg/kg single dose (~7-12 g for a 70 kg adult); the sleep-deprivation benefit used ~150 mg/kg.
compounds.retail_dose: 500 mg-1 g per serving of L-tyrosine - roughly 7-20x below the effective per-kg trial dose.
compounds.population_studied: Healthy adults under acute stress: military trainees, sleep-deprived subjects, cold/altitude exposure, high cognitive load (Jongkees 2015 review, J Psychiatr Res; Military Medicine 2015 rapid evidence assessment).
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No - explicitly does NOT improve cognition in unstressed, rested, catecholamine-replete adults. Benefit requires temporary dopamine/noradrenaline depletion.
compounds.funding_split: Much of the supportive work is military/government-funded (independent), which is a strength; the limitation is small samples and narrow stressor conditions, not industry bias.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not applicable - no single-study pooled effect; the literature is a set of small task-specific trials.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No major advisory; caution with MAOIs and hyperthyroidism.
compounds.not_a_supplement: For focus lost to sleep deprivation the real fix is sleep; tyrosine only blunts, not reverses, the deficit.
compounds.conditional_on: Benefit conditional on an acute catecholamine-depleting stressor (sleep deprivation, cold, sustained high load) AND a per-kg dose far above retail.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for everyday focus. Tyrosine only helps when catecholamines are being depleted by an acute stressor - sleep deprivation, cold, noise, sustained multitasking. compounds.largest_independent_trial: Vaucher et al. 2012 CMAJ, n=198 women, independent (Swiss academic) - positive but modest. IV-iron blood-donor RCT (PMC7449957) was NULL for fatigue despite raising ferritin.

compounds.retail_dose: Ferrous sulfate 325 mg = ~65 mg elemental; ferrous bisglycinate 'gentle' products 18-28 mg elemental
compounds.population_studied: Non-anemic menstruating women aged 18-53 with unexplained fatigue and ferritin <50 ug/L (Vaucher, Verdon). Some blood-donor and athlete cohorts.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No. Benefit is repletion of a deficit; an iron-replete healthy adult gets no energy benefit and iron accumulates.
compounds.funding_split: not reported as a formal subgroup; key positive trials are academic/independent
compounds.outlier_leverage: Effect rests heavily on the single positive Vaucher trial; the null IV-iron donor trial cuts the other way.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: FDA: iron is the leading cause of fatal pediatric poisoning; single-ingredient iron carries mandatory warnings. Excess iron/unmonitored supplementation is harmful. No efficacy advisory.
compounds.movement_note: Prior conditional structure holds. Scored 4 (not 5) for the FATIGUE-specific claim because the effect rests on one modest positive trial and a null IV trial; correcting frank iron-deficiency anemia is a 5, feeling 'more energy' in mild low-ferritin is a 4.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Identify and treat the cause of iron loss (heavy menses, GI bleeding, malabsorption); dietary iron. Iron is a targeted deficiency correction, not an energy product.
compounds.conditional_on: Serum ferritin <30-50 ug/L (iron deficiency without anemia). Collapses to ~1 if ferritin is normal.
compounds.verdict: Buy ONLY if serum ferritin is low. In iron-deficient menstruating women (ferritin <50 ug/L, no anemia) oral iron produces a real, modest reduction in fatigue. In iron-replete adults it does nothing for energy and adds overdose/GI risk. Test ferritin before buying; do not take blind.

Krayenbuehl 2011 Blood 118:3222 (IV iron, ferritin<50 women)

compounds.trial_count: 16 RCTs in the fatigue/cognition meta, but ~0 informative fatigue RCTs in non-deficient adults
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Markun 2021 Nutrients systematic review/meta-analysis (independent) - concluded evidence for fatigue in non-deficient people is essentially absent.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Markun 2021 meta-analysis (16 RCTs, 6276 participants) found NO reliable fatigue benefit in non-deficient populations; only a single eligible fatigue study, insufficient to pool. No clinically meaningful energy effect established.
compounds.clears_mcid: No - no measurable fatigue effect to clear an MCID in replete adults. na in deficiency (repletion is corrective).
compounds.trial_dose: Deficiency correction: 1000 ug oral/day or IM injections; marketed energy dose 500-5000 ug with no fatigue evidence
compounds.retail_dose: 1000 ug cyanocobalamin typical (~40,000% RDA); 'energy' sublinguals/shots 2500-5000 ug
compounds.population_studied: Mostly older adults and mixed clinical cohorts; almost no eligible RCTs in non-deficient people with fatigue.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No. Benefit is entirely repletion of a deficit; megadoses in replete people are renally excreted.
compounds.funding_split: not applicable - no positive body of trials to split
compounds.outlier_leverage: not applicable
compounds.regulatory_advisory: none found for efficacy; B12 is safe but that is not the same as effective.
compounds.movement_note: Prior confirmed exactly. The conditional IS the category: 5 to correct true deficiency, 1 as a generic energy product.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Treat the cause of deficiency (diet, pernicious anemia, metformin/PPI review). For non-deficient fatigue: sleep, screen for anemia/thyroid/depression.
compounds.conditional_on: Documented B12 deficiency (low serum B12 or elevated methylmalonic acid/homocysteine).
compounds.verdict: Do NOT buy for energy unless you are actually B12-deficient. In deficiency (pernicious anemia, vegans, metformin/PPI users, malabsorption) repletion is a 5. In replete people - which is most tired people - B12 does nothing; the 'energy shot' is theatre. Test B12/MMA first.
primary_sources: LiverTox/clinical reviews of B12 repletion

compounds.trial_count: 16 RCTs (cognition meta) plus a large ergogenic literature
compounds.total_n: ~492 in the cognition meta; thousands in the ergogenic literature
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Xu 2024 Front Nutr meta-analysis (independent, PRISMA) - positive but modest and somewhat equivocal for cognition.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Xu 2024 (Front Nutr, 16 RCTs, n=492): significant but modest SMDs for memory, attention and processing speed; Digit test d=0.77. Gordji-Nejad 2024 (Sci Rep): single 0.2 g/kg dose attenuated - not abolished - sleep-deprivation cognitive decline, peak ~4 h.
compounds.clears_mcid: For strength/power: yes. For 'mental energy'/fatigue in rested adults: marginal; several cognition endpoints are equivocal.
compounds.trial_dose: 3-5 g/day maintenance (20 g/day loading); cognition trials often 5-20 g/day; sleep-deprivation study 0.2 g/kg single dose (~14-18 g)
compounds.retail_dose: 5 g/day (standard scoop) - matches muscle dosing, at the LOW end of cognition dosing
compounds.population_studied: Healthy adults, athletes, sleep-deprived subjects, vegetarians (larger effect), some clinical cohorts.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Partly. Ergogenic/muscle benefit transfers strongly; anti-fatigue/cognitive benefit shows up mainly under stressors (sleep loss, vegetarian diet, high mental load).
compounds.funding_split: not a clean split; effect survives in independent academic work, so not funding-driven
compounds.outlier_leverage: Cognition pooled effect is heterogeneous across small trials; no single dominating outlier, but wide CIs.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: none found; long safety record. Trivial water-weight gain and benign creatinine rise (can confound eGFR).
compounds.movement_note: Held near prior (4 -> 3.5). Docked half a point because the specific 'energy/anti-fatigue' claim (vs strength) is condition-dependent and cognition effects are modest/equivocal; retail 5 g under-doses the cognition trials.
compounds.not_a_supplement: For fatigue from sleep debt, the fix is sleep, not creatine; creatine only blunts the decline.
compounds.conditional_on: Meaningful 'energy' effect strongest under sleep deprivation, in vegetarians, or during high cognitive/physical demand; less in a well-rested omnivore.
compounds.verdict: Buy if the goal is strength/power/muscle (that evidence is a 5) or resilience under sleep deprivation/stress. As a general 'energy' or anti-fatigue supplement for a rested healthy adult, the effect is real but small and condition-dependent - a 3.5, not the miracle marketing implies. Cheap and safe, so low downside.
primary_sources: Kreider 2017 JISSN position stand

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Population transfer — the fatigue benefit exists only in diseased/fatigued cohorts; the healthy-adult subgroup was non-significant (g=-0.351, CI -0.756 to +0.053, p=0.089), so it does not transfer to the marketed "energy for healthy adults" use.
compounds.trial_count: 13 RCTs (fatigue meta); 7 RCTs (statin myopathy 2024 meta)
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Taylor 2015 Atherosclerosis, RCT in confirmed statin myopathy - independent, NULL.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Tsai 2022 fatigue meta (13 RCTs, n=1126): pooled SMD favors CoQ10 but across highly heterogeneous clinical populations. Statin myopathy: 2024 meta (7 RCTs, n=389) positive in only 4/7; Taylor 2015 RCT in CONFIRMED statin myopathy found NO benefit on pain, strength or exercise capacity despite raised serum CoQ10.
compounds.clears_mcid: Unclear/no in most settings; the confirmed-myopathy RCT is a clean null.
compounds.trial_dose: 100-600 mg/day (fatigue and statin trials)
compounds.retail_dose: 100-200 mg/day (ubiquinone); ubiquinol 100 mg
compounds.population_studied: Statin users, fibromyalgia, chronic fatigue, CKD, heart failure, older adults - NOT healthy energetic adults.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No. Any signal is in depleted/diseased states; healthy adults are not CoQ10-limited.
compounds.funding_split: Not formally split, but positive fatigue trials skew small and industry-adjacent; the cleanest independent RCT is null.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Pooled fatigue effect depends on heterogeneous small trials; statin-myopathy 'signal' hinges on 4 of 7 trials.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: none found; well tolerated. Higher doses raise serum levels without translating to muscle/energy benefit (Taylor).
compounds.movement_note: Prior confirmed. is_compromised=true: any positive grade leans on heterogeneous small/industry-adjacent trials and a statin-myopathy result that flips to null in the cleanest independent RCT.
compounds.not_a_supplement: For statin muscle symptoms the evidence-based options are dose reduction, statin switch, or intermittent dosing - not CoQ10.
compounds.conditional_on: At best a trial in statin-associated muscle symptoms or a documented mitochondrial/deficiency state - not general tiredness.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for general energy. 'Fatigue' benefit is concentrated in specific patient groups (fibromyalgia, CKD, heart failure, statin users) in small, heterogeneous, often industry-adjacent trials, and even the statin-myopathy evidence is split. No credible energy benefit in a healthy adult.
primary_sources: Tsai 2022 fatigue meta, PMC9449413
CoQ10 statin myopathy 2024 meta, PMC12554813
Taylor 2015 Atherosclerosis (confirmed statin myopathy RCT)

compounds.largest_independent_trial: None on the blends.
compounds.effect_size_ci: No credible whole-product RCT with an energy outcome. Effect size unknown.
compounds.clears_mcid: No - no outcome data exist to clear anything.
compounds.trial_dose: n/a - the finished multi-herb products are not tested
compounds.retail_dose: Proprietary blend totals often 300-1000 mg split across 5-10 herbs = tens of mg each, far below any single-herb trial dose
compounds.population_studied: None for the blends as sold; evidence is borrowed from single-herb studies at doses the blends rarely deliver.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No basis to claim transfer; the products themselves are untested.
compounds.funding_split: not applicable
compounds.outlier_leverage: not applicable
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Blends frequently contain ashwagandha (see TGA liver advisory) and undisclosed stimulant amounts; 'proprietary blend' labeling obscures actual doses.
compounds.movement_note: Prior confirmed. Absence of finished-product evidence plus proprietary-blend under-dosing keeps this at 1.

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Funding-source subgroup / independence (Check 1), reinforced by regulatory safety signal (Check 7)
compounds.trial_count: Multiple small RCTs, majority manufacturer-affiliated
compounds.total_n: Low hundreds per outcome, fragmented across sponsor-linked trials
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Genuinely independent, adequately powered fatigue RCTs are scarce; the influential energy/QoL data are KSM-66/Ixoreal-linked.
compounds.effect_size_ci: KSM-66 trials report ~+18% 'energy/fatigue' and +15% QoL subscale improvements, but as secondary outcomes in sponsor-linked studies. Dose-response meta-analysis: benefit on stress and anxiety with LOW certainty (GRADE); no robust independent fatigue effect size.
compounds.clears_mcid: Unclear - subjective self-report changes with no established fatigue MCID and high placebo response in this literature.
compounds.trial_dose: 300 mg twice daily (KSM-66) or 600 mg/day root extract, 8 weeks
compounds.retail_dose: 300-600 mg/day standardized extract - matches trial dose
compounds.population_studied: Mostly stressed or anxious healthy adults; fatigue/energy is typically a secondary, subjective outcome, not the primary endpoint.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Weak. Effects are in stressed/anxious cohorts; a 'more energy' claim in a healthy adult is not independently established.
compounds.funding_split: Positive results concentrate in industry/manufacturer-affiliated trials; independent evidence is sparse and weaker.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Small-trial, high-placebo literature; pooled stress/anxiety effects are low-certainty and sensitive to study choice.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: TGA (Feb 2024): risk of liver injury - 12 reports, 4 hospitalizations, onset 6 weeks-22 months; Netherlands Pharmacovigilance (2023/2025) additional cases; NIH LiverTox lists ashwagandha hepatotoxicity. India/AYUSH disputes causality.
compounds.movement_note: New graded entry. is_compromised=true: the energy/fatigue signal depends on manufacturer-linked trials with subjective secondary endpoints, and a regulatory liver-injury signal caps any recommendation.
compounds.not_a_supplement: For stress-driven fatigue: sleep, exercise, and evidence-based stress management; if genuinely anxious, seek diagnosis rather than an OTC hepatotoxicity risk.
compounds.conditional_on: Any modest benefit is really an anti-stress/anxiety effect in stressed people, not a primary energy effect.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for energy. The fatigue/energy signal comes almost entirely from manufacturer-linked (KSM-66/Ixoreal) trials with subjective secondary endpoints; independent replication is thin and certainty is graded LOW. There is now a regulatory liver-injury signal. Downside outweighs a weak, industry-driven benefit.
primary_sources: TGA safety advisory: Withania somnifera and rare liver injury (2024)
NIH LiverTox NBK548536 (Ashwagandha)
Ashwagandha stress/anxiety dose-response meta-analysis (low-certainty GRADE)
KSM-66 QoL/energy RCTs (Ixoreal-affiliated)

compounds.trial_count: A handful of small RCTs plus a heterogeneous meta-analysis
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Chen 2010 J Altern Complement Med (Cs-4 in older adults) - small, modest positive.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Chen 2010 (Cs-4, healthy older adults): modest VO2max/ventilatory-threshold gains in a small RCT. C. militaris acute crossover (2025 PLOS One): raised resting VO2 and faster reaction time - acute, small n. Fungal-supplement meta (2025): 'potential' endurance benefit, heterogeneous, low quality. No pooled fatigue effect with tight CIs.
compounds.clears_mcid: Unclear - small samples, surrogate endpoints (VO2, reaction time), not a validated energy/fatigue MCID.
compounds.trial_dose: Cs-4 fermentation product 3-4.5 g/day for 6-12 weeks; C. militaris acute 1 g standardized extract
compounds.retail_dose: ~1 g/day mushroom/mycelium (often low active content) - typically below the 3-4.5 g Cs-4 trial dose
compounds.population_studied: Small groups of older adults, recreational athletes; some acute crossover work.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Weak/uncertain; some data in older adults and athletes but small and inconsistent.
compounds.funding_split: Many trials TCM/manufacturer-linked; independent replication limited.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Heterogeneous small trials; meta conclusions are fragile and quality is low.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: none prominent for efficacy; wild Cordyceps and some products carry heavy-metal/adulteration concerns. Effective doses (3-4.5 g Cs-4) exceed typical retail 1 g.
compounds.movement_note: New graded entry at 2: real but thin, small, heterogeneous evidence on surrogate endpoints, and retail under-dosing.
compounds.not_a_supplement: For aerobic capacity, structured endurance training is the intervention with a real effect size.
compounds.conditional_on: Possible marginal ergogenic effect at 3-4.5 g/day Cs-4 - not at typical 1 g retail doses.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for energy. Endurance/VO2max signals come from small, short, often industry- or TCM-linked trials with inconsistent results, and retail products under-dose the trials. No convincing energy benefit in a healthy adult.

C. militaris acute crossover 2025 PLOS One, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0351725
Fungal supplementation endurance meta-analysis 2025, PMC12631420

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Check 5 - population transfer / mechanism (withdrawal-reversal vs net enhancement)
compounds.trial_count: Dozens of RCTs and multiple meta-analyses
compounds.largest_independent_trial: McLellan 2016 (Neurosci Biobehav Rev) comprehensive independent review; 2025 acute-attention meta-analysis - both positive.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Consistent dose-related improvements in alertness, vigilance, reaction time and fatigue ratings up to ~300 mg (McLellan 2016 review; 2025 attention meta-analysis shows significant gains in reaction time and accuracy). Non-linear: benefit plateaus and side effects rise above ~300-400 mg.
compounds.clears_mcid: Yes - alertness/vigilance improvements are perceptible and behaviorally meaningful, especially under fatigue.
compounds.trial_dose: ~40-300 mg (single dose); ~3-6 mg/kg for ergogenic effect
compounds.retail_dose: 100-200 mg per coffee/tablet/energy product - within the effective range
compounds.population_studied: Healthy adults, sleep-deprived subjects, shift/military personnel, athletes - broad and independent.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Yes - directly demonstrated in healthy and sleep-deprived adults.
compounds.funding_split: Effect is robust across independent (military/academic) work, not industry-dependent.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Effect is consistent, not outlier-driven.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: FDA warns against pure/highly concentrated powdered caffeine (fatal overdose risk); EFSA: up to 400 mg/day habitual safe for most adults, 200 mg in pregnancy. Non-linear dose-response: low-moderate doses give most of the benefit, higher doses add anxiety/tachycardia/sleep disruption.
compounds.section3_prior_score: n/a (added - the category's true positive control)
compounds.movement_note: Added because grading 'Energy' without caffeine omits the only agent with strong independent outcome data. Scored 5 for acute alertness/fatigue, with the honest caveat that it is a stimulant (tolerance/withdrawal), not a nutrient.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Caffeine is a drug/stimulant, not a nutritional supplement; it manages symptoms of fatigue and cannot substitute for adequate sleep.
compounds.conditional_on: Largest net benefit in the non-tolerant or sleep-deprived; habitual users partly chase withdrawal relief.
compounds.verdict: This is the one 'energy' agent that actually works. Large independent literature: reliable, dose-related reduction in fatigue and improvement in alertness, vigilance and reaction time, in both rested and sleep-deprived adults. Caveat: it is a stimulant with tolerance and withdrawal, not a nutrient - benefit is largely restoring, not exceeding, baseline in habituated users.
primary_sources: McLellan 2016 Neurosci Biobehav Rev 71:294, doi:10.1016/j.neubiorev.2016.09.001
Acute caffeine on attention meta-analysis 2025, doi:10.1007/s00213-025-06775-1
Caffeine and cognition in sleep deprivation, NCBI NBK209050

compounds.retail_dose: 200-500 mg/day, standardization highly variable/unverified

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Check 2 (outlier / single-RCT leverage): the RCT base is one statistically-criticized trial (ONTRAC) plus a failed replication (ONTRANS) and a 2024 meta-analysis finding pooled evidence insufficient
compounds.trial_count: 1 pivotal phase 3 RCT (ONTRAC) + 1 phase 3 RCT in transplant recipients (ONTRANS, null) + 1 large independent retrospective cohort (2025 VA, n=33,822)
compounds.total_n: ONTRAC n=386; ONTRANS n=158; VA cohort n=33,822 (12,287 exposed)
compounds.largest_independent_trial: 2025 Veterans Affairs retrospective cohort (VA Corporate Data Warehouse), 33,822 patients / 12,287 nicotinamide-exposed: HR 0.86 any new skin cancer, HR 0.78 SCC — independent, supports ONTRAC in high-risk patients.
compounds.effect_size_ci: ONTRAC: 23% relative reduction in new NMSC, rate ratio 0.77 (95% CI 0.63-0.95, P=0.02); SCC -30%, BCC -20% (NS); AK -11% to -20%. VA cohort: HR 0.86 any skin cancer, HR 0.78 for SCC (0.44 if started after first cancer), BCC HR 1.00 (no effect).
compounds.clears_mcid: Yes for the chemoprevention endpoint — a ~1 in 4 reduction in new skin cancers is clinically meaningful in a high-risk population. NA for cosmetic outcomes (never measured).
compounds.trial_dose: 500 mg twice daily = 1000 mg/day for 12 months
compounds.retail_dose: Nicotinamide/niacinamide capsules commonly labeled 500 mg once daily (500 mg/day) — half the trial dose; many 'B3' products are nicotinic acid (niacin), the wrong molecule.
compounds.population_studied: Immunocompetent adults with >=2 histologically confirmed nonmelanoma skin cancers in the prior 5 years (ONTRAC); large VA cohort of veterans with prior keratinocyte cancer. NOT tested for cosmetic/anti-aging endpoints.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No. Benefit is confined to high-risk skin-cancer patients; no evidence it helps a healthy adult's skin, and ONTRANS shows it does NOT work in immunosuppressed transplant recipients.
compounds.funding_split: ONTRAC funded by Australia's NHMRC (independent/government); 2025 VA cohort is independent. Not an industry-funding artifact.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not applicable — pivotal RCT plus a large independent cohort concur; effect is not driven by one study.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No efficacy advisory; JAAD 2025 safety reviews note nicotinamide is well tolerated (distinct from niacin — no flushing).
compounds.not_a_supplement: For general skin health/appearance the effective interventions are broad-spectrum sunscreen, sun avoidance/protective clothing, and dermatologic surveillance — not a B3 pill.
compounds.conditional_on: Applies only to immunocompetent patients with a prior nonmelanoma skin cancer, at 500 mg BID. Does not apply to transplant/immunosuppressed patients (ONTRANS null) or to cosmetic use.
compounds.verdict: Buy ONLY if you are a high-risk immunocompetent patient with a prior nonmelanoma skin cancer, and dose it correctly at 500 mg TWICE daily. This is a chemoprevention drug-like use, not a cosmetic/anti-aging supplement — there is essentially no credible evidence it improves the appearance of healthy skin.
primary_sources: Chen AC et al. A Phase 3 Randomized Trial of Nicotinamide for Skin-Cancer Chemoprevention (ONTRAC). NEJM 2015;373:1618-1626. PMID 26488693
Allen NC et al. Nicotinamide for Skin-Cancer Chemoprevention in Transplant Recipients (ONTRANS). NEJM 2023;388:804-812. PMID 36856616. DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2203086
2025 Veterans Affairs retrospective cohort, nicotinamide and keratinocyte carcinoma (n=33,822); reported AJMC/News-Medical Sep 2025
JAAD Reviews 2025: Examining the safety of nicotinamide for skin cancer prevention. S2950-1989(25)00079-0

compounds.trial_count: Multiple small RCTs and open-label studies (systematic reviews pool ~10-20 studies); no large hard-endpoint RCT
compounds.total_n: Individual trials typically 20-60 subjects; no large pooled hard-outcome trial
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Thin — the most robust data (healthy-adult MED RCTs; El Mansouri 2023 xeroderma pigmentosum RCT) are small and frequently manufacturer-linked; no large independent hard-endpoint trial.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Surrogate endpoints only: RCTs report subjects markedly more likely to increase MED and reduce erythema (one healthy-adult RCT reported ~22x higher odds of MED increase vs placebo); a 2025 red-orange+PLE RCT reported +23.8% MED and -46.2% erythema intensity. No wrinkle/skin-cancer hard-endpoint RCT.
compounds.clears_mcid: Uncertain/likely no in isolation — a fractional MED increase is far below the protection of an SPF 30-50 sunscreen; no defined MCID and no hard-outcome data.
compounds.trial_dose: 240 mg once or twice daily (240-480 mg/day), often started ~15 days before sun exposure
compounds.retail_dose: Heliocare and equivalents are 240 mg capsules dosed 240-480 mg/day — retail matches trial dose.
compounds.population_studied: Healthy adults (MED/erythema studies) and patients with photodermatoses (polymorphic light eruption, solar urticaria), melasma, and xeroderma pigmentosum. Mostly small, short trials.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Partially — MED/erythema studies are in healthy adults, so the surrogate effect transfers, but real-world value over proper sunscreen use is unproven.
compounds.funding_split: Not cleanly split in a meta-analysis, but a large share of trials are authored by or affiliated with the manufacturer (Industrial Farmaceutica Cantabria / IFC, Fernblock). Independent replication is limited.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not formally assessed; small heterogeneous trials on surrogate endpoints.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None found (efficacy or safety) from TGA/EMA/FDA/MHRA.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Primary evidence-based sun protection is topical broad-spectrum SPF 30-50+ sunscreen, shade, and UPF clothing. Note nicotinamide, by contrast, shows NO MED effect — different mechanism, not interchangeable.
compounds.conditional_on: Value is greatest as an adjunct in diagnosed photodermatoses/melasma alongside sunscreen; not as monotherapy sun protection.
compounds.verdict: Conditional / low priority. Real but modest photoprotective signal on surrogate endpoints (raises MED, blunts UV erythema). It is an ADJUNCT, never a substitute for sunscreen, and most of the literature comes from the manufacturer. Reasonable add-on for photodermatoses/melasma under a dermatologist; not worth buying as stand-alone sun defense.

compounds.trial_count: 23 RCTs (AmJMed 2025 meta-analysis); overlapping set re-analyzed by Batool 2026
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Independent, high-quality studies in the AmJMed 2025 pool showed no significant effect on hydration, elasticity, or wrinkles — the benefit is confined to industry-funded and low-quality trials.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Batool 2026 primary pooled: hydration SMD 0.44 (95% CI 0.15-0.73), elasticity SMD 0.62 (95% CI 0.15-1.10), TEWL -0.39 (95% CI -0.62 to -0.16). After removing high-leverage outliers: wrinkle effect non-significant; hydration and elasticity diminished. Week-8 heterogeneity fell from I2=79.2% to 40.4% on outlier removal.
compounds.clears_mcid: No for wrinkles (effect disappears in sensitivity/independent analysis). Borderline for hydration/elasticity — statistically present but small and attenuated once outliers/funding are controlled.
compounds.trial_dose: Skin RCTs used ~2.5-10 g/day hydrolyzed collagen (distinct from the 15-30 g used in tendon studies)
compounds.retail_dose: Retail skin collagen 2.5-10 g/day — matches the skin-trial dose (the dose-shortfall trap applies to tendon/joint collagen, not skin dosing).
compounds.population_studied: Predominantly women 35-65 with visible photoaging; short (8-12 week) trials.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Marginal — studied in mild photoaging; any residual hydration benefit is small and cosmetic, not structural.
compounds.funding_split: AmJMed 2025 (23 RCTs, n=1474): industry-funded studies POSITIVE; non-industry-funded studies showed NO benefit for hydration, elasticity, or wrinkles. High-quality studies showed NO significant effect on any endpoint; only low-quality studies showed an elasticity gain.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Yes — Batool 2026: pooled wrinkle/roughness/dermal-density effects were driven by high-leverage outlier studies; excluding them removed the wrinkle effect and roughly halved heterogeneity.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None found; the issue is efficacy/bias, not safety.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Evidence-based anti-aging: daily broad-spectrum sunscreen, topical retinoids, and topical moisturizers/humectants.
compounds.conditional_on: Any defensible claim is limited to modest short-term skin hydration; the wrinkle/anti-aging claim is not supported.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for wrinkles. Two 2025/2026 meta-analyses show the anti-wrinkle claim is a funding-source-and-outlier artifact: it survives pooled analysis but vanishes in independent and high-quality studies, and collapses when one outlier study is removed. A modest hydration/elasticity signal is the only thing that partly survives, and even that shrinks.

compounds.largest_independent_trial: Thin — most robust trials are small and frequently industry-affiliated; no large independent RCT.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Meta-analysis: elasticity SMD 0.77 (95% CI 0.19-1.35, I2=75%, p=0.009); moisture SMD 0.53 (95% CI 0.05-1.01, I2=52%, p=0.03); wrinkle depth NOT significantly reduced.
compounds.clears_mcid: Unclear — moderate instrument effects from short trials with high heterogeneity; no established MCID and wrinkle depth (the outcome consumers care about) is null.
compounds.trial_dose: 2-12 mg/day (most 4-9 mg/day)
compounds.retail_dose: Retail astaxanthin 4-12 mg/day — matches trial dosing.
compounds.population_studied: Healthy adults (often middle-aged, several Japanese-population trials); 6-12 week durations.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Yes for the studied endpoints (healthy adults), but magnitude and durability beyond 12 weeks are unknown.
compounds.funding_split: No clean meta-analysis funding subgroup, but several included trials are authored/funded by AstaReal / Fuji Chemical Industry (dominant ingredient supplier). Independent replication limited; treat pooled effect with caution.
compounds.outlier_leverage: High heterogeneity (I2 up to 75%) suggests the pooled elasticity effect may be sensitive to individual studies; no formal leave-one-out analysis reported.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None found from TGA/EMA/FDA/MHRA.
compounds.movement_note: Nudged 2 -> 2.5 (below the 1-point flag threshold): a formal meta-analysis shows consistent significant elasticity/moisture effects, slightly above pure marketing, though still small, industry-heavy, and wrinkle-null.
compounds.not_a_supplement: For photoaging: daily broad-spectrum sunscreen and topical retinoids remain the higher-evidence interventions.
compounds.conditional_on: Any claim should be limited to modest hydration/elasticity, not wrinkle reduction.
compounds.verdict: Weak buy at best. A meta-analysis shows statistically significant but small improvements in skin elasticity and moisture and NO effect on wrinkle depth, from small, short (6-12 week) trials with heavy involvement from the ingredient maker (AstaReal/Fuji) and high heterogeneity. Signal is real but fragile.

compounds.trial_count: ~4-6 small RCTs plus a 2025 larger RCT (n=150)
compounds.total_n: Most trials 40-129; 2025 sodium hyaluronate RCT n=150
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Thin — the largest recent trials still involve the manufacturer; no large fully independent RCT.
compounds.effect_size_ci: 120 mg/day x12 wk RCTs report significant improvement in wrinkle assessment, stratum corneum hydration, TEWL, and elasticity; 2025 n=150 RCT reports significant gains in dermal density, hydration, elasticity, epidermal thickness, and wrinkle depth. Effect sizes/CIs inconsistently reported across the small trials.
compounds.clears_mcid: Uncertain — instrument-measured improvements are statistically significant but small; no established MCID, and visible clinical relevance is modest.
compounds.trial_dose: 120 mg/day (range 120-240 mg/day), various molecular weights (2 kDa to ~300-400 kDa)
compounds.retail_dose: Retail oral HA commonly 100-200 mg/day — matches the studied 120 mg dose.
compounds.population_studied: Healthy adults with dry skin/wrinkles, predominantly Japanese cohorts aged ~22-60; 8-12 week trials.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Yes for the studied endpoints (healthy adults), but generalizability beyond Japanese cohorts and beyond 12 weeks is untested.
compounds.funding_split: No formal meta subgroup, but the core hydration/wrinkle evidence comes largely from authors employed by Kewpie Corporation (Hyabest ingredient); a 2025 trial was manufacturer-funded (Ritual) with Kewpie supplying HA. Independent confirmation thin.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not formally assessed; small heterogeneous trials.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None found from TGA/EMA/FDA/MHRA.
compounds.movement_note: Nudged 2 -> 2.5 (below the 1-point flag threshold): several concordant positive RCTs including a 2025 n=150 trial exceed pure marketing, but funding concentration keeps it low.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Topical humectants/moisturizers (including topical HA) and daily sunscreen are the higher-evidence, cheaper route to skin hydration.
compounds.conditional_on: Best-supported claim is modest short-term skin hydration; wrinkle claims rest on manufacturer-linked trials.
compounds.verdict: Weak/conditional. Multiple RCTs at 120 mg/day for 12 weeks report improved hydration, elasticity, and reduced wrinkle depth, but the positive evidence is concentrated in trials authored or funded by the ingredient maker (Kewpie), in small, ethnically narrow (Japanese) samples, and whether oral HA reaches the skin in humans is unresolved. Real signal, shaky foundation.

compounds.trial_count: No credible RCTs for skin/hair/nails in non-deficient people; brittle-nail evidence = ~3 small studies without placebo controls
compounds.largest_independent_trial: None of adequate quality; dermatology reviews (JAAD 2022) confirm the lack of RCTs.
compounds.effect_size_ci: No reliable placebo-controlled effect size exists for skin/hair/nails in non-deficient adults.
compounds.clears_mcid: No — there is no credible controlled effect to clear any MCID.
compounds.trial_dose: Case/series doses vary (e.g., 2.5 mg/day for nails) but were uncontrolled
compounds.retail_dose: Retail biotin 5,000-10,000 mcg (5-10 mg) — 150-300x the ~30 mcg adequate intake; megadose with no efficacy rationale and clear assay-interference risk.
compounds.population_studied: Efficacy data limited to case reports and small uncontrolled series, mostly in genuine deficiency or specific genetic/nail-fragility conditions. No adequate placebo-controlled RCT in healthy, non-deficient adults.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No. Any benefit is confined to correcting true deficiency; supplementation in replete/healthy adults has no demonstrated benefit.
compounds.funding_split: Not applicable — no body of RCTs to split; the problem is absence of evidence, not funding bias.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not applicable.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: FDA Safety Communication (2017, updated 2019): high-dose biotin interferes with immunoassays via the biotin-streptavidin system, causing falsely low troponin (one patient death reported), and false thyroid (FT4/FT3 high, TSH low, mimicking Graves) and hCG results. AACC/ADLM guidance echoes this. Lives in the safety literature, not the efficacy literature.
compounds.not_a_supplement: For hair/skin/nails address the actual cause (iron/ferritin, thyroid, protein/caloric adequacy, androgenetic alopecia treatment); biotin is not the fix in non-deficient people.
compounds.conditional_on: Only justified to correct a laboratory-confirmed biotin deficiency; discontinue >=48-72 h before blood tests to avoid assay interference.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for skin/hair/nails unless you have a documented, genuine biotin deficiency (rare). No credible RCT shows benefit in non-deficient adults, and it actively causes dangerous laboratory-test interference — including falsely low troponin (a reported death) and false thyroid results. Actively worse than inert.

compounds.trial_count: ~30+ RCTs; ~6 combined-therapy RCTs in the key pooled analysis
compounds.largest_independent_trial: WHI (Jackson 2006, NEJM, PMID 16481635), NIH-funded, n=36,282: no significant overall hip-fracture reduction, +kidney stones.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Yao 2019 (6 RCTs, n=49,282): hip fracture RR ~0.84 (favouring). WHI (Jackson 2006, n=36,282): overall hip fracture HR 0.88 (0.72-1.08, NS); 21% lower in age 60+ and ~29% in adherent. Zhao 2017 (33 RCTs, n=51,145 community-dwelling): hip fracture RR 1.09 (0.85-1.39), NS.
compounds.clears_mcid: Yes in frail/institutionalized elderly (absolute hip-fracture reduction meaningful); No/near-null in community-dwelling adults.
compounds.trial_dose: 1000-1200 mg elemental calcium + 400-800 IU vitamin D3 daily (WHI 1000 mg Ca + 400 IU D; Decalyos 1200 mg Ca + 800 IU D)
compounds.retail_dose: 500-600 mg elemental calcium per pill (often 1000-1200 mg/day) + 800-1000 IU D3 - broadly in trial range
compounds.population_studied: Mostly women 65+, many institutionalized or vitamin-D-deficient/low calcium intake; some healthy postmenopausal (WHI).
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Poor. Benefit is a repletion/frailty effect, not a general one; healthy replete community-dwelling adults get little to nothing.
compounds.funding_split: No clean funding-source split published; the decisive split is by population (institutional/deficient vs community-dwelling), not by funder.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Pooled hip-fracture signal leans heavily on Decalyos (Chapuy) institutionalized cohorts; remove institutional trials and the community-dwelling estimate is null.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No efficacy advisory, but WHI showed a 17% increase in kidney stones; calcium-alone CV/MI signal (Bolland) is contested. Not a withdrawal-level flag.
compounds.movement_note: Nudged down 0.5. Prior credited a ~15% total-fracture reduction; primary sources show the hip-fracture benefit (Yao 2019 pooled HR ~0.84) is driven by institutionalized/deficient cohorts and DISAPPEARS in community-dwelling adults (Zhao 2017 JAMA, 33 RCTs, null). The marketed population and the benefiting population differ.
compounds.not_a_supplement: For community-dwelling adults the fall/fracture lever is progressive resistance + balance/impact training (e.g. LIFTMOR); dietary calcium beats pills.
compounds.conditional_on: Institutionalization, age 70+, low dietary calcium intake, or documented vitamin D deficiency (25-OH-D low). Not for replete healthy adults.
compounds.verdict: Conditional buy. Real hip-fracture reduction exists but is concentrated in institutionalized, low-intake, or vitamin-D-deficient elderly (Chapuy/Decalyos, French nursing homes). In healthy community-dwelling adults the effect is near-null, so for the typical retail buyer it is weak. Get calcium from diet first; supplement adds kidney-stone risk.

compounds.trial_count: 16 RCTs in 2022 meta (BMD); fracture RCTs few and mostly MK-4
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Knapen MHJ et al. 2013, n=244 healthy postmenopausal Dutch women - the largest well-conducted MK-7 BMD RCT; modest, not fracture-powered.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Knapen 2013 (n=244, 180 mcg MK-7, 3 yr): significant but small attenuation of lumbar-spine and femoral-neck BMD loss vs placebo (P<0.05), no effect at total hip. 2022 meta (16 RCTs, n=6425): lumbar BMD improved (P=0.006); fracture reduction driven by low-quality MK-4 Japanese trials.
compounds.clears_mcid: Marginal. Lumbar BMD gains (~+0.02 g/cm2) are below what would reliably translate to fracture prevention.
compounds.trial_dose: MK-7 180 mcg/day (Knapen); fracture-signal trials used MK-4 45,000 mcg/day (45 mg, pharmacological)
compounds.retail_dose: MK-7 ~90-180 mcg/day
compounds.population_studied: Postmenopausal women (osteopenia/osteoporosis); much of the fracture data is Japanese osteoporotic women on MK-4 45 mg.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Weak. Studied in bone-losing postmenopausal women, not healthy mixed-sex adults; effect absent in mixed-sex studies.
compounds.funding_split: Not cleanly reported; several MK-7 BMD trials (MenaQ7/NattoPharma) are ingredient-supplier linked.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Yes - pooled fracture/BMD benefit is leveraged by Japanese MK-4 45 mg trials; excluding them shrinks the effect toward null.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None found (K2 is well tolerated; caution with warfarin due to antagonism).
compounds.movement_note: Held at 2.5. Primary sources confirm the prior: biomarkers move, BMD moves marginally (lumbar), hard endpoints barely, effect concentrated in postmenopausal women and largely on MK-4 drug doses not MK-7.
compounds.conditional_on: Postmenopausal women with existing bone loss; benefit at retail MK-7 dose is unproven for fractures.
compounds.verdict: Do not rely on it for fractures. Biomarkers (osteocalcin carboxylation) move robustly and lumbar BMD attenuation is real but small; hard fracture evidence is weak and concentrated in older Japanese MK-4 45 mg/day pharmacological trials, a dose ~250x the retail MK-7 pill. As a bone insurance policy it is thin.

compounds.largest_independent_trial: Groenendijk I et al. systematic review/meta-analysis 2022 (PMID 34666201) - no significant fracture reduction.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Groenendijk 2022 meta (RCT arm): fracture RR 0.72 (0.51-1.02), NS; significant reductions in serum ALP and osteocalcin (turnover markers). Dietary meta (Farsinejad-Marj 2016): + association with hip/femoral-neck BMD.
compounds.clears_mcid: No - no significant clinical fracture endpoint; turnover-marker changes are surrogate.
compounds.trial_dose: ~300-600 mg elemental Mg/day in the small RCTs
compounds.retail_dose: Magnesium glycinate/citrate labelled '400-500 mg' typically delivers ~60-100 mg elemental Mg per serving (glycinate ~14% elemental)
compounds.population_studied: Older adults, osteoporotic/osteopenic; much evidence is dietary-intake observational, not supplement RCT.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Poor for the replete. Plausible only in low-intake individuals (poor diet, PPIs, malabsorption, alcohol).
compounds.funding_split: Not reported (too few RCTs).
compounds.outlier_leverage: Small trial base; borderline fracture trend is fragile to any single study.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None specific to bone; high doses cause diarrhoea, caution in renal impairment.
compounds.movement_note: Down 0.5. Primary look shows no statistically significant fracture RCT result (RR 0.72, 0.51-1.02) and BMD signal is largely observational/dietary, so the honest grade sits at deficiency-correction only.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Adequate dietary magnesium (greens, legumes, nuts, whole grains) and treating the cause of deficiency.
compounds.conditional_on: Documented or likely magnesium deficiency (low intake, PPI/diuretic use, malabsorption).
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for bones unless deficient. No RCT shows fracture reduction (pooled RR 0.72, CI crosses 1). Bone-turnover markers shift and observational BMD associations are positive, but that is mechanism plus epidemiology, not outcome. Any real benefit is a correction-of-deficiency effect.

compounds.trial_count: 3 mega-RCTs + numerous smaller; consistent
compounds.largest_independent_trial: VITAL - LeBoff MS et al. NEJM 2022;387:299-309 (PMID 35939577), NIH-funded, n=25,871: null for fractures.
compounds.effect_size_ci: VITAL (LeBoff 2022, n=25,871): total fracture HR 0.98 (0.89-1.08), hip HR 1.01 (0.70-1.47) - null; no effect on falls or BMD/structure. D-Health (n=21,315): fractures null. Burt 2019 (n=311): radial vBMD change -1.2% (400 IU) vs -2.4% (4000) vs -3.5% (10000), dose-dependent LOSS.
compounds.clears_mcid: No - null for fractures/falls in replete adults; where it moves BMD at high dose it moves it the WRONG way.
compounds.trial_dose: VITAL 2000 IU/day; D-Health 60,000 IU/month (~2000 IU/day); Burt compared 400 vs 4000 vs 10000 IU/day
compounds.retail_dose: 1000-5000 IU/day common; many products 5000 IU which sits in the harm-signal zone at long term
compounds.population_studied: Generally healthy, largely vitamin-D-replete midlife/older adults not selected for deficiency or low bone mass.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: It IS the healthy-adult population - and the answer is no benefit; deficiency-repletion benefit does not transfer to replete adults.
compounds.funding_split: VITAL and D-Health are government/independently funded and null, removing any funding-artifact defence.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not applicable - null result is consistent across three independent mega-trials.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No withdrawal, but the dose-response harm (Burt 2019) plus hypercalcemia/stone risk at high dose is a real check-6 signal; supraphysiologic dosing is discouraged.
compounds.movement_note: Down 0.5. Adding the dose-response harm signal (Burt 2019: 4000/10000 IU lowered radial/tibial BMD vs 400 IU) on top of the three null mega-trials makes standalone D for replete adults a near-1.5, not a 2.
compounds.not_a_supplement: For fall/fracture prevention in the replete: resistance + balance training; correct true deficiency with modest (800-1000 IU) dosing, not megadoses.
compounds.conditional_on: Genuine deficiency (25-OH-D <25-30 nmol/L) / osteomalacia, or frail institutionalized elderly (then combine with calcium).
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for bones if you are vitamin-D-replete. Three mega-trials (VITAL, D-Health, DO-HEALTH; >65,000 people) are null for fractures and falls, and high doses actively LOWERED bone density in a dose-dependent way. Value is limited to correcting genuine deficiency/osteomalacia, ideally paired with calcium in frail elderly.
