compounds.trial_count: 0 fracture RCTs for citrate; 2 major RCTs for ranelate (SOTI, TROPOS)
compounds.largest_independent_trial: None independent for citrate. Ranelate: Meunier PJ et al. (SOTI) NEJM 2004;350:459-468 (PMID 14749454) - industry-funded drug trial.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Ranelate SOTI (Meunier 2004, n=1649): vertebral fracture RR 0.59 (0.48-0.73), ~41% reduction. TROPOS: nonvertebral reduction. Strontium citrate: NO RCT effect size exists.
compounds.clears_mcid: N/A for citrate (no data); ranelate cleared it but is unsafe/withdrawn.
compounds.trial_dose: Ranelate 2 g/day (SOTI/TROPOS). Retail citrate typically 680 mg elemental strontium/day - no dose has fracture evidence.
compounds.retail_dose: ~340-680 mg elemental strontium/day (citrate)
compounds.population_studied: Ranelate: postmenopausal women with osteoporosis (SOTI/TROPOS). Citrate: essentially unstudied in humans for fracture or BMD.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No transfer - efficacy compound is a withdrawn drug, not the retail supplement, and not tested in healthy adults.
compounds.funding_split: Ranelate trials were Servier-sponsored; irrelevant to citrate, which has no trials.
compounds.outlier_leverage: The apparent citrate 'BMD benefit' is a DEXA artifact (~10% BMD overestimate per 1% strontium incorporated), not a real gain.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: EMA/PRAC restricted strontium ranelate (Apr 2013), recommended suspension (2014) for +4 serious cardiac and +4 thrombosis events per 1000 patient-years; marketing authorisation withdrawn 2020. Applies to the drug, but signals the element's cardiovascular concern.
compounds.movement_note: Held at 1. Primary sources reinforce it: the only efficacy data are for ranelate (a withdrawn drug), citrate is untested, and its apparent DEXA benefit is an artifact.
compounds.not_a_supplement: The only agent that reduced fractures was a prescription drug (strontium ranelate), now withdrawn for cardiovascular safety - not something to replicate with OTC citrate.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy. The fracture evidence belongs to a DIFFERENT compound - prescription strontium ranelate (SOTI/TROPOS) - which the EMA restricted then withdrew for cardiovascular and clot risk. Over-the-counter strontium CITRATE has zero fracture RCTs, zero BMD RCTs, and any 'BMD gain' on a DEXA is largely a measurement artifact (strontium's high atomic number inflates the reading).

compounds.trial_dose: 1000-1200 mg elemental calcium/day
compounds.retail_dose: 500-600 mg elemental calcium per pill (carbonate ~40% elemental, citrate ~21%)
compounds.population_studied: Postmenopausal women / older adults (WHI, Bolland meta-analyses).
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Weak; benefit limited to low-intake individuals, and downside risks apply broadly.
compounds.funding_split: Not the crux; the CV-risk debate is methodological (per-protocol vs ITT) rather than funding-driven.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not the deciding issue here; consistency is the problem, not a single outlier.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Kidney-stone increase (WHI); ongoing regulatory/guideline caution about calcium-supplement CV signal (contested, e.g. Bolland BMJ 2010/2011).
compounds.not_a_supplement: Dietary calcium (dairy, fortified foods, greens); load-bearing exercise for bone strength.
compounds.conditional_on: Low dietary calcium intake; even then prefer diet + vitamin D pairing.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy standalone for bones. Calcium-only supplements give small BMD changes, weak/inconsistent fracture reduction, raise kidney-stone risk, and carry a contested cardiovascular/MI signal. compounds.trial_count: 1 RCT (n=131) + 1 open-label follow-up
compounds.largest_independent_trial: None independent; only König DA et al. Nutrients 2018;10(1):97 (PMID 29337906), industry-funded.
compounds.effect_size_ci: König 2018 (n=131): spine vBMD +4.2%, femoral neck +7.7% vs placebo over 12 mo - effect size implausibly large for a nutritional agent.
compounds.clears_mcid: Nominally yes, but the effect size is large enough to raise validity concerns rather than confidence.
compounds.trial_dose: 5 g specific collagen peptides (FORTIBONE)/day for 12 months
compounds.retail_dose: Generic collagen powders 5-10 g/day, usually NOT the specific FORTIBONE peptide studied

compounds.regulatory_advisory: None found.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Progressive resistance and impact/loading exercise (e.g. LIFTMOR trial) has stronger BMD evidence in postmenopausal women.
compounds.conditional_on: Would need independent replication and fracture outcomes before any recommendation.

compounds.compound: Collagen / gelatin + vitamin C, dosed 30-60 min pre-load (timing protocol)
compounds.trial_count: 8 structural/adaptation RCTs (n=257) + a handful of small tendinopathy RCTs (Praet n=20; combination-product trials)
compounds.largest_independent_trial: No large independent clinical trial exists. The independent mechanistic/structural work (Shaw 2017 n=8; Lis & Baar dose-finding; various n=8-24 adaptation studies) is small; positive but underpowered for clinical endpoints.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Shaw 2017 (AJCN, PMID 27852613): 15 g gelatin + 48 mg vit C ~doubled the serum collagen-synthesis marker PINP vs placebo (crossover, n=8). Systematic review (JFMK 2026;11:130): tendon CSA +6-11% vs +1-4% placebo in 3/4 RCTs; stiffness +15.4% to +56.4%, Young's modulus +14.2% to +46.2% in the 15-30 g arms (narrative synthesis, no pooled SMD). Praet 2019 (Nutrients 11:76): VISA-A rose +12.6 (9.7-15.5) on collagen vs +5.3 (2.3-8.3) on placebo over 3 mo, all on top of a calf-loading program.
compounds.clears_mcid: Partial. VISA-A gain of ~12.6 exceeds the ~7-point MCID, but that trial is small and industry-funded. Structural CSA/stiffness changes are real but no trial has shown they translate to a hard clinical endpoint (re-injury rate, return-to-sport, tendon rupture).
compounds.trial_dose: 15-30 g/day hydrolyzed collagen peptides OR vitamin-C-enriched gelatin, with >=50 mg vitamin C, taken ~30-60 min before loading. Structural benefits (CSA, stiffness) appeared only at 15-30 g; 5-15 g did not move stiffness.
compounds.retail_dose: Typically 2.5-10 g collagen peptides per serving (vitamin C often 50-90 mg where included). Many marine/beauty collagen products are 2.5-5 g - well under the 15 g structural threshold.
compounds.population_studied: 8 RCTs, n=257 (246 M : 11 F), ages 18-52, mostly trained/active young men; plus small mid-portion Achilles tendinopathy cohorts (Praet 2019, n=20) and patellar tendon studies. Very little data in women, older adults, or untrained people.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Only partially - adaptation shown in trained young men and requires concurrent heavy loading; does not imply benefit for a sedentary adult taking collagen without training.
compounds.funding_split: Structural systematic review (JFMK 2026) reported no industry funding for its included adaptation trials, and the CSA/stiffness signal carries the grade. The clinical pain/function signal is weaker: the supplement+physiotherapy meta-analysis (J Clin Med 2022;11:1666) pooled pain SMD = -0.74 (95% CI -1.37 to -0.10) but 2/6 trials were pharma-funded, I2=77%, and function was null (SMD 0.29, 95% CI 0.00-0.58). The flagship Achilles trial (Praet/TENDOFORTE) used Gelita-supplied peptides.
compounds.outlier_leverage: The pooled clinical pain estimate is fragile - wide CI whose upper bound (-0.10) nearly touches null, driven by high heterogeneity and small trials. The structural estimate is more robust (consistent direction across independent labs).
compounds.regulatory_advisory: none found
compounds.not_a_supplement: Progressive / heavy-slow resistance loading is the primary stimulus for tendon adaptation and remission of tendinopathy; the supplement is at best a timing-optimized adjunct to it.
compounds.conditional_on: Only works when layered on structured high-intensity resistance loading (>=70% 1RM), taken ~30-60 min pre-load, at 15+ g with vitamin C. Inert without training and likely underdosed at typical retail servings.
compounds.verdict: Conditional buy, and only as an adjunct. The strongest claim - that 15-30 g collagen/gelatin + vitamin C ~60 min before loading increases tendon cross-sectional area and stiffness - is GRADE A but exists ONLY layered on structured high-intensity resistance loading, in mostly young healthy men, at doses above what most retail tubs deliver. The consumer-facing endpoints (pain, function, injury reduction) rest on small, largely Gelita-funded trials. Without training it does close to nothing.

compounds.total_n: Effectively zero in controlled standalone human tendon trials.
compounds.largest_independent_trial: None. Largest rigorous work is preclinical (rat Achilles, n=30, 20/40/200 mg/kg) showing histologic/biomechanical healing - does not transfer to a grading of human outcomes.
compounds.effect_size_ci: No standalone human tendon RCT with an effect size to report. Combination curcumin+Boswellia open-label study reported symptom reduction with no control group. Any pain benefit in the physiotherapy+supplement meta (SMD -0.74) is confounded by co-ingredients and pharma funding.
compounds.clears_mcid: na - no controlled human tendon endpoint exists to compare against an MCID.
compounds.trial_dose: Human combination studies ~500-2000 mg/day curcuminoids, usually with bioavailability enhancers (piperine, phytosome/Meriva) or Boswellia; animal studies 20-200 mg/kg.
compounds.retail_dose: 500-1500 mg turmeric extract per serving, often 95% curcuminoids; formulation (phytosome, piperine) varies widely and drives both absorption and hepatotoxic risk.
compounds.population_studied: Predominantly animal models (rat Achilles collagenase injury, 20-200 mg/kg). Human data limited to open-label / post-observational tendinopathy cohorts using combination products.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No - no human tendon outcome data in any population, healthy or injured.
compounds.funding_split: The only positive human tendon-adjacent signals come from combination-product studies, some industry-linked; no independent standalone RCT exists to split.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not applicable - no pooled human tendon estimate exists.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: TGA safety advisory 15 Aug 2023: turmeric/curcumin medicines linked to rare liver injury - 18 reports, 9 probable, 2 severe including 1 fatality; risk higher with enhanced-bioavailability formulations. Health Canada (Dec 2025) called for mandatory liver-warning labels; LiverTox lists turmeric as a cause of hepatotoxicity.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Loading-based tendinopathy rehabilitation; NSAIDs short-term for the inflammatory component if needed.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for tendon health. There is no credible standalone human tendon-outcome RCT. Every positive human data point is either an open-label observational study or a curcumin+Boswellia combination product; the rest is rat collagenase and cell-culture work. Mechanism (NF-kB, anti-inflammatory) massively outruns outcome. There is also an active regulatory liver-injury signal.

compounds.trial_count: 1 reasonable-quality RCT (Sandford) + small essential-fatty-acid/antioxidant combination trials in tendon disorders.
compounds.total_n: ~70-140 across the usable rotator cuff trials.
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Sandford et al. (BMJ Open Sport Exerc Med 2018), rotator cuff related shoulder pain: transient SPADI improvement at 3 mo, null at 12 mo.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Sandford 2018 (BMJ Open Sport Exerc Med): SPADI -8.3 (95% CI -15.6 to -0.94, p=0.03) favouring omega-3 at 3 months; NO between-group difference at 12 months. CI upper bound near zero.
compounds.clears_mcid: Borderline/no. SPADI MCID is ~8-13 points; the -8.3 point estimate sits at the lower edge, the CI crosses toward null, and the effect is not durable.
compounds.trial_dose: ~1.5-2.5 g/day combined EPA+DHA (Sandford: ~1530 mg EPA + 1035 mg DHA); some rotator cuff work used up to 2.4 g/day EPA+DHA over 12 weeks.
compounds.retail_dose: Standard fish-oil softgel delivers ~300 mg EPA + 200 mg DHA (~500 mg combined) per capsule; hitting the ~1.5-2.5 g trial dose needs 3-5 capsules/day, which most users do not take.
compounds.population_studied: Rotator cuff related shoulder pain / rotator cuff tendinopathy patients (Sandford RCT, plus small chronic tendon-disorder athlete trials). Not healthy adults and not a tendon-structure or rupture-healing population.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No - benefit was a pain reduction in symptomatic rotator cuff patients, not a structural or preventive effect in healthy tendons.
compounds.funding_split: No clear industry-funding artifact in the primary Sandford trial (academic/KCL); the broader supplement+physio pooled pain estimate that includes omega-3 combos is partly pharma-funded and heterogeneous (I2=77%).
compounds.outlier_leverage: Single-trial evidence base, so the grade hinges on one modest, non-durable result rather than a pooled outlier.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Dose-response safety signal: high-dose omega-3 (>=1 g/day, notably ~4 g icosapent/EPA-DHA in STRENGTH and OMEMI) is associated with increased atrial fibrillation risk - relevant given tendon trial doses sit in the 1.5-2.5 g range.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Progressive tendon loading / exercise rehabilitation for the specific tendinopathy; short-term analgesia if needed.
compounds.conditional_on: Any modest benefit is specific to rotator cuff related shoulder pain and to the first ~3 months; requires ~1.5-2.5 g/day EPA+DHA.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for tendons. The single decent RCT (rotator cuff related shoulder pain) showed a modest, statistically borderline pain benefit at 3 months that had vanished by 12 months and sits around or below the SPADI MCID. It is a transient anti-inflammatory effect in a pain population, not evidence of tendon healing, and typical retail softgels underdose the trial.

compounds.effect_size_ci: Preliminary rotator cuff repair study: a non-significant trend toward improved healing with vitamin C; no reported effect size clearing significance. No standalone tendinopathy pain/function RCT.
compounds.clears_mcid: No - the one human tendon signal did not reach statistical significance, let alone an MCID.

compounds.funding_split: Not applicable - no positive controlled human tendon result to split by funding.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not applicable - no pooled estimate.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: none found (high-dose ascorbate broadly safe; oxalate/kidney-stone risk at gram doses is the main caveat, not a tendon-specific advisory).
compounds.movement_note: New in-category compound; no Section 3 prior.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Progressive tendon loading plus adequate dietary protein and vitamin C; correct any true deficiency.

compounds.verdict: Do not buy as a standalone tendon product. Vitamin C is a genuine cofactor for prolyl hydroxylase in collagen synthesis, but the only human tendon trial (rotator cuff repair) showed a non-significant trend, and there is no evidence that high-dose vitamin C helps tendons in already-replete adults. compounds.retail_dose: 1500 mg/day glucosamine (HCl or sulfate); retail matches trial dose, so under-dosing is not the failure mode.

compounds.not_a_supplement: Exercise/resistance loading and weight loss (for overweight patients) outperform glucosamine on OA pain and function.

compounds.verdict: Do not buy. The combination does not beat placebo on pain overall (-0.5 cm/10 cm, below MCID); the only positive signals are an exploratory moderate-to-severe subgroup in GAIT and an industry non-inferiority-vs-celecoxib trial with no placebo arm.

compounds.largest_independent_trial: Debbi EM et al. 2011 (n=50, 6 g/day): significantly greater pain and function improvement vs placebo at 12 weeks, but small and short.
compounds.effect_size_ci: 2025 NMA (Kim 2006 + Debbi 2011): WOMAC pain WMD -10.1 (95% CI -19.1 to -1.07), function -14.1 (-22.9 to -5.35), stiffness -16.2 (-26.8 to -5.60) on 0-100 WOMAC. Kim 2006 (n=50): significant on function/total, NOT on pain or stiffness subscales.
compounds.clears_mcid: Borderline/uncertain. Wide CIs from tiny trials; point estimates approach WOMAC MCID (~15-20/100) only for stiffness, lower bound near zero for pain.
compounds.trial_dose: 3-6 g/day (Kim 1.125 g x3; Debbi 3 g x2 = 6 g/day).
compounds.retail_dose: Retail commonly 1-2 g/day (often bundled in low-dose joint blends), below the 3-6 g/day used in positive trials.
compounds.population_studied: Adults with mild-to-moderate knee OA; trials 12 weeks only.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Weak. One trial in mild knee pain (Xu 2023) showed small QoL benefit; no data for healthy joint maintenance.
compounds.funding_split: No funding-source meta-split available; several trials supplied product by manufacturers. Too few trials to test industry interaction.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Pooled effect rests on just two 50-patient trials; either dropping out would destabilize it.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No specific regulator efficacy/safety advisory; generally well tolerated (GI upset).
compounds.not_a_supplement: Exercise and weight management remain the higher-evidence interventions.
compounds.verdict: Weak buy-case at best. Nominally positive on pain and function, but the entire evidence base is a handful of small (n<50/arm), short (12-week) trials with industry ties and no large independent replication. Signal without confirmation.

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Check 1 - Funding-source subgroup: 100% of efficacy RCTs are manufacturer-sponsored, no independent replication exists
compounds.trial_count: 2-3 small RCTs (Crowley 2009 n=52; Lugo 2016 n=191; Tjandra 2023 n=102), all sponsor-linked.
compounds.largest_independent_trial: None truly independent. Lugo 2016 (largest, n=191) funded by InterHealth Nutraceuticals (now Lonza), the ingredient manufacturer; Crowley 2009 (UC-II 33% vs G/C 14% WOMAC drop) also industry-sponsored, n=52.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Lugo 2016 (n=191, 3-arm): UC-II 40 mg/day reduced total WOMAC ~40% from baseline vs less for placebo. BUT 2025 NMA placed UC-II (Lugo 2016) LAST across pain/function/stiffness (pain SUCRA 0.03), i.e. no advantage over placebo in the pooled network.
compounds.clears_mcid: Unclear/likely no. Within-arm percentage drops look large but the between-arm placebo-controlled ranking is bottom-tier.
compounds.trial_dose: 40 mg/day UC-II (delivering ~10 mg undenatured type II collagen).
compounds.retail_dose: 40 mg/day UC-II (matches trial dose); dosing is not the weakness.
compounds.population_studied: Adults with symptomatic knee OA (Lugo 2016) or exercise-related knee discomfort in healthy subjects (Lugo 2013); 90-180 days.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Marginal. One small industry trial in healthy exercising adults (Lugo 2013) claimed less knee discomfort; not independently confirmed.
compounds.funding_split: No independent trial exists to split against. The entire efficacy claim is manufacturer-funded; the one independent pooled reanalysis (2025 NMA) is null-to-worst.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Whole category leverages sponsor trials; independent pooling erases the effect.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No specific regulator advisory; safety appears benign.
compounds.movement_note: Held near prior but nudged down to 2.0: the 2025 independent NMA (UC-II ranked last, pain SUCRA 0.03) undercuts the sponsor-trial narrative; move is 0.5, so flag not set.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Resistance exercise for knee OA.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy on current evidence. The positive trials are all manufacturer-funded, and a 2025 independent network meta-analysis ranked UC-II LAST of all supplements for pain (SUCRA 0.03) and function. The marketing (beats glucosamine+chondroitin) rests on tiny industry studies.

Crowley DC et al. Int J Med Sci 2009;6:312 (PMID 19847319)

Tjandra O et al. Indones Biomed J 2023

compounds.trial_count: 15-20+ RCTs; multiple 2022-2025 meta-analyses and a 2025 turmeric-products NMA (17 studies, PMID 40731001).
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Mix of independent and sponsor trials; several academic trials (e.g., Panahi 2014, n=53, Iran) positive but small and often product-supplied. No single large fully-independent pivotal trial; effect is consistent across many small ones.
compounds.effect_size_ci: 2025 NMA: curcumin WOMAC pain WMD -3.31 (95% CI -5.25 to -1.34), total WOMAC -15.6 (-23.5 to -7.61), function -11.7 (-17.8 to -5.52). 2022 meta-analysis (PMC9353077): significant VAS and WOMAC pain reduction, non-inferior to NSAIDs. Non-inferiority vs paracetamol in bioavailable-turmeric RCT (PMC7847013).
compounds.clears_mcid: Plausibly yes for pain in enhanced-extract trials (VAS reductions ~1.5-2 cm in several studies exceed MCID), but heterogeneous and formulation-dependent.
compounds.trial_dose: Standardized curcuminoids ~1000-1500 mg/day, or bioavailability-enhanced extracts (Meriva 1000 mg, BCM-95 500 mg x2, Theracurmin), often with piperine.
compounds.retail_dose: Generic turmeric capsules/powder deliver curcuminoids at low, poorly-absorbed doses; without an enhanced-delivery matrix, retail active exposure falls well below the trial extracts.
compounds.population_studied: Adults with symptomatic knee OA; trials typically 4-16 weeks.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No OA-prevention data in healthy adults; benefit is symptomatic in established knee OA.
compounds.funding_split: Many trials used or were supported by extract manufacturers (Indena/Meriva, Arjuna/BCM-95); no clean funding-split meta-analysis, but effect persists across independent academic RCTs, unlike glucosamine.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Effect is distributed across many small trials rather than one outlier, which strengthens it; but small-study/publication bias likely inflates the pooled estimate.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: TGA safety alert (2023): turmeric/curcumin products linked to liver injury (18 reports, 9 probable, 2 severe including 1 fatal); US DILIN and USP reviews document idiosyncratic hepatotoxicity, risk amplified by piperine and high-absorption formulations.
compounds.conditional_on: Efficacy applies to bioavailability-enhanced standardized extracts, not plain turmeric spice/powder. Avoid piperine-boosted high-dose products given the hepatotoxicity signal; monitor LFTs if used long-term.
compounds.verdict: Conditional. Best-supported item in the category: multiple RCTs show real pain reduction, roughly non-inferior to NSAIDs/paracetamol. But effect sizes come from bioavailability-enhanced extracts (Meriva, BCM-95, Theracurmin), many trials are industry-funded and short, and there is a genuine regulator liver-injury signal. Plain retail turmeric powder is not the studied product.
primary_sources: Zeng L et al. Front Immunol 2022;13:891822 (PMC9353077)
2025 turmeric-products NMA, BMC Complement Med Ther (PMID 40731001)
Bioavailable turmeric vs paracetamol RCT (PMC7847013)
TGA safety alert: turmeric/curcumin liver injury, 2023
Panahi Y et al. 2014

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Funding-source / independence (Check 1), reinforced by a null independent meta-analysis

compounds.trial_dose: 5-Loxin 100-250 mg/day (30% AKBA) or Aflapin 100 mg/day; standardized high-AKBA extracts.
compounds.retail_dose: Generic Boswellia 300-500 mg capsules are often low-AKBA (2.5-10% boswellic acids), not the standardized 30%-AKBA extracts used in trials; typical retail active AKBA falls below trial exposure.
compounds.population_studied: Adults with knee OA; trials 30-90 days, small samples.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No prevention data; symptomatic OA only.
compounds.funding_split: No funding-split meta-analysis exists because independent trials are nearly absent; virtually all positive data are sponsor-generated.
compounds.outlier_leverage: The headline NMA pain effect (-22.4) rests on ONE 38-patient sponsor trial; extreme leverage.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No specific regulator efficacy advisory; generally tolerated (mild GI), but standardization of retail products is inconsistent.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Exercise and weight management.
compounds.conditional_on: Any benefit is tied specifically to standardized high-AKBA extracts (5-Loxin/Aflapin), not generic low-standardization Boswellia.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy on current evidence. Reported effect sizes are large, but they come almost entirely from very small trials run or funded by the ingredient manufacturers (Laila/PLThomas), with essentially no independent replication. The signal is real-looking but compromised.

compounds.trial_count: 26 RCTs in the 2024 dose-response meta (Cruz-Sanabria); 19 RCTs/1683 subjects in Ferracioli-Oda 2013
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Wade 2007/2010 prolonged-release melatonin in adults >=55 (Neurim-funded); independent pediatric/DSWPD trials (Gringras MENDS 2017 n=146) confirm circadian use.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Sleep onset latency WMD -7.06 min (95% CI -9.75 to -4.37; Ferracioli-Oda 2013). Prolonged-release: subjective SOL -6.30 min, objective SOL -5.05 min (2023 meta, n=4875). Total sleep time +8-13 min. Dose-response peaks ~4 mg.
compounds.clears_mcid: For insomnia: NO - a 5-7 min SOL reduction sits below the ~10-min MCID; a null in a suit. For circadian phase disorders: YES - phase-shifting is the mechanism, not the minutes.
compounds.trial_dose: 0.5-5 mg; phase-shift work uses 0.5 mg; insomnia trials 2-5 mg PR
compounds.retail_dose: 3-10 mg immediate-release (typically ABOVE the effective circadian dose; gummies often overshoot)
compounds.population_studied: Mixed: primary insomnia adults, DSWPD, jet-lag travelers, children with ASD/ADHD, elderly. Effect is population-specific.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Poor as a hypnotic for a healthy non-circadian-disrupted adult; strong for a healthy traveler crossing time zones.
compounds.funding_split: not reported as a formal subgroup; effect not funding-dependent
compounds.outlier_leverage: Pooled SOL effect robust across many trials; not one-study-driven.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: UK MHRA: prescription-only medicine (Circadin), not an OTC supplement. US OTC potency unregulated - Erland & Saxvig found actual content 83% below to 478% above label; CDC MMWR 2022: US pediatric melatonin ingestions rose >500% 2012-2021.
compounds.not_a_supplement: For chronic insomnia the first-line guideline treatment is CBT-I (AASM/ACP), not melatonin.
compounds.conditional_on: Grade of 4+ applies only to circadian indications (DSWPD, jet lag, shift work, child/ASD). For adult primary insomnia it is closer to 2.5.
compounds.verdict: Buy for the RIGHT problem: circadian misalignment (delayed sleep-wake phase disorder, jet lag, shift work, non-24, ASD/child sleep). For garden-variety adult primary insomnia it is a weak agent the AASM recommends AGAINST. Use LOW dose (0.5-1 mg) timed hours before target sleep for phase-shifting; high-dose 5-10 mg products are chronobiologically wrong.
primary_sources: Ferracioli-Oda E 2013, PLoS One, PMID 23691095 (DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0063773)
Cruz-Sanabria F 2024, J Pineal Res, PMID 38888087 (DOI 10.1111/jpi.12985)
Sateia MJ 2017 AASM Clinical Practice Guideline, J Clin Sleep Med (weak recommendation AGAINST melatonin for chronic insomnia)
Gringras P 2017 MENDS RCT, J Am Acad Child Adolesc Psychiatry
Erland LAE & Saxvig 2017 J Clin Sleep Med (label-content analysis)

compounds.trial_count: ~3 RCTs in the elderly meta (Mah 2021); one 2024 bisglycinate RCT

compounds.clears_mcid: Borderline/NO - the elderly SOL figure would clear MCID but rests on low-quality trials; the healthy-adult d=0.2 does not.
compounds.trial_dose: 500 mg elemental Mg/day (Abbasi 2012, as oxide); ~200 mg elemental as bisglycinate (Rawji 2024)
compounds.retail_dose: ~90-100 mg elemental Mg (a '500 mg magnesium glycinate' capsule is mostly glycine by mass)
compounds.population_studied: Older adults with insomnia (Abbasi 2012); healthy adults reporting poor sleep (Rawji 2024). Benefit skews to low-baseline-intake subgroups.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Poor transfer to a magnesium-replete healthy adult; closer to correcting a shortfall than a sleep drug.
compounds.funding_split: not reported
compounds.outlier_leverage: Elderly pooled effect leans heavily on Abbasi 2012, a single small trial.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: none found; high doses cause osmotic diarrhea.
compounds.conditional_on: Meaningful benefit conditional on low dietary magnesium / relative deficiency (subgroup effect in Rawji 2024).
compounds.verdict: Weak, condition-dependent. A reasonable low-risk trial IF dietary magnesium is low; do not expect a hypnotic effect in a replete adult. Effect sizes are small and the older-adult meta-analysis is explicitly rated substandard by its own authors.

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Check 3 (effect size vs MCID / subjective-vs-objective split): objective polysomnographic endpoints are null, so the only positive signal lives in a subjective dichotomous outcome prone to response bias.
compounds.trial_count: Bent 2006 meta: 16 RCTs; 2020 review: 60 studies; 2024 umbrella review of prior meta-analyses

compounds.clears_mcid: NO - objective sleep parameters show no reliable clinically meaningful change.
compounds.trial_dose: 300-900 mg extract at night
compounds.retail_dose: 300-600 mg extract (variable valerenic-acid content; poor batch standardization)
compounds.population_studied: Mixed insomnia/poor-sleep adults; highly heterogeneous extracts and doses.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No reliable effect to transfer.
compounds.funding_split: Not formally split; heterogeneity, extract-quality variance, and industry trials drive the unstable positive older results.

compounds.regulatory_advisory: Generally good safety (rare hepatotoxicity in multi-herb products); no efficacy-based advisory.
compounds.not_a_supplement: CBT-I is the evidence-based route for chronic insomnia.

Older positive meta-analyses rest on a subjective dichotomous 'improved sleep?' outcome, heterogeneous and poorly standardized extracts, and industry involvement. Good safety is not the same as working.

compounds.conditional_on: Any grade above 2 conditional on using high-dose concentrate, not pills/gummies.
compounds.verdict: Thin and small-study-driven. A few small trials show more sleep time/efficiency and raised urinary melatonin, but samples are tiny (n=8-20), some industry-linked, and a 2024 RCT in overweight/obese adults was null. High-anthocyanin juice concentrate was tested; retail gummies/capsules are nowhere near that dose.
primary_sources: Howatson G 2012, Eur J Nutr, DOI 10.1007/s00394-011-0263-7
Losso JN 2018, Am J Ther, PMID 28901974 (n=8 PSG pilot)
Pigeon WR 2010, J Med Food, PMID 20438325
2024 Nutrients tart cherry powder RCT, MDPI 2072-6643/16/23/4125 (null)

compounds.trial_count: 5 RCTs in Cheah 2021 meta (n=400)
compounds.largest_independent_trial: No large independent (non-manufacturer) RCT identified - the central weakness.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Pooled SMD on overall sleep -0.59 (95% CI -0.75 to -0.42; Cheah 2021). Larger in the insomnia subgroup, dose >=600 mg/day, >=8 wk. HAM-A anxiety and sleep-onset latency improved (Langade 2019/2021).
compounds.clears_mcid: Plausibly yes on PSQI in the insomnia subgroup, but confounded by uniform industry funding.
compounds.trial_dose: 300-600 mg/day root extract (KSM-66), 6-10 wk
compounds.retail_dose: 300-600 mg KSM-66 - retail matches trial dose
compounds.population_studied: Adults with insomnia/stress, largely Indian trial sites; healthy stressed adults.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Uncertain; sleep effect strongest in insomnia, weaker/soft in healthy adults.
compounds.funding_split: No independent-only pooled estimate exists - the SMD -0.59 is effectively an industry-funded pooled result (Ixoreal supplied material in the key trials). That is the compromise.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Small meta; a couple of Langade trials carry the effect.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: TGA safety advisory (2024) + second alert (2026) on Withania somnifera and very rare liver injury; MHRA Yellow Card hepatotoxicity reports; Netherlands Lareb alerts 2023/2025 (12 cases to mid-2025); WHO VigiBase 15 hepatobiliary reports (Dec 2023); NIH LiverTox monograph. Some cases required hospitalization; most resolved on withdrawal.
compounds.conditional_on: Any benefit conditional on 600 mg/day, >=8 wk, diagnosed insomnia; and on accepting the liver-signal risk (avoid with hepatic disease, other hepatotoxins, alcohol).
compounds.verdict: Conditional and safety-flagged. Meta-analysis shows a moderate sleep effect, but essentially all trials are industry-funded (Ixoreal/KSM-66), single-region, and short. More important: multiple regulators (TGA 2024 and 2026, MHRA Yellow Card, Netherlands Lareb, NIH LiverTox) have posted liver-injury signals. Efficacy is real-ish; the risk-benefit for a sleep aid is unattractive.
primary_sources: Cheah KL 2021, PLoS One, PMID 34559859 (DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0257843; 5 RCTs, SMD -0.59)
Langade D 2019/2021, Cureus / J Ethnopharmacol S0378874120331585 (KSM-66, Ixoreal-supplied)
TGA 2024/2026 safety advisory 'Withania somnifera (Ashwagandha) and very rare risk of liver injury'
NIH LiverTox, NBK548536

compounds.trial_count: A handful of small RCTs
compounds.largest_independent_trial: No convincing independent PSG trial; no direct evidence of human BBB crossing.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Modest reductions in sleep latency and small non-REM/EEG changes in small trials (100-300 mg); one Western RCT reported sleep-efficiency and HRV improvement. No robust PSG replication; CIs not meaningful given size.
compounds.clears_mcid: NO / unclear - endpoints soft and small.
compounds.trial_dose: 100-300 mg (PharmaGABA)
compounds.retail_dose: 100-750 mg - retail meets or exceeds trial dose (dose is not the limiter; the BBB is)
compounds.population_studied: Small Japanese RCTs; sedentary overweight women (one Western RCT); healthy adults.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Weak; a central effect is biochemically implausible at oral doses.
compounds.funding_split: No formal split, but the supportive trials cluster around the PharmaGABA manufacturer (Pharma Foods).
compounds.outlier_leverage: Small, sponsor-linked studies carry the claim.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: none found
compounds.verdict: Do not buy. Oral GABA poorly crosses the blood-brain barrier; the small positive sleep RCTs are largely industry-funded (PharmaGABA/Pharma Foods), soft-endpoint, and any effect likely runs through peripheral gut-vagal signaling, not central inhibition. Mechanism outruns outcome.
primary_sources: Yamatsu A 2016, J Nutr Sci Vitaminol (PharmaGABA sleep latency)
Byun JI 2018, J Clin Neurol (GABA/5-HTP combination - confounded by co-ingredient)
Boonstra E 2015, Front Psychol (review: oral GABA BBB uncertainty)

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Effect size vs MCID (check 3), reinforced by population transfer (check 5)
compounds.trial_count: ~10 clinical trials in 2024 meta (n=772); key insomnia pilot Zick 2011
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Zick SM 2011 (rigorous, placebo-controlled, primary insomnia) - NULL.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Zick 2011 (270 mg chamomile BID x28 d, n=34): NO significant difference vs placebo in total sleep time, sleep efficiency, latency, WASO, or quality. 2024 meta: significant PSQI reduction but across heterogeneous populations and low study quality.
compounds.clears_mcid: NO in primary insomnia (null); questionable in the positive elderly subgroups.
compounds.trial_dose: 270-540 mg standardized extract/day, or ~400-1600 mg chamomile; apigenin content low and variable
compounds.retail_dose: 'Apigenin 50 mg' pills or chamomile tea (~1-2 mg apigenin/cup) - far below any pharmacologic exposure
compounds.population_studied: DSM-IV primary insomnia (Zick, null); elderly nursing-home residents and postpartum women (positive).
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No transfer to a healthy adult with insomnia (best insomnia RCT null).
compounds.funding_split: Not formally split; the positive meta is dominated by low-quality, heterogeneous trials.
compounds.outlier_leverage: PSQI meta-effect leans on a few positive special-population studies (nursing home, postpartum).
compounds.regulatory_advisory: none found; allergy risk in Asteraceae-sensitive individuals.
compounds.conditional_on: Any signal conditional on elderly/postpartum populations, not general adult insomnia.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for insomnia. The best-designed primary-insomnia RCT (Zick 2011) was flatly NULL on every sleep-diary measure. Positive results are in special populations (elderly nursing-home, postpartum) and heterogeneous low-quality meta-analyses. Isolated apigenin has essentially no direct human sleep outcome data - it is a mechanism (GABA-A ligand), not a proven product.
primary_sources: Zick SM 2011, BMC Complement Altern Med, PMID 21939549 (DOI 10.1186/1472-6882-11-78; NULL primary-insomnia RCT)
Abdullahzadeh M 2017 (elderly nursing-home, positive)
2024 chamomile-on-sleep meta-analysis, PMID 39106912

compounds.trial_count: 1-2 stand-alone RCTs + combination trials
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Singapore older-adult 5-HTP RCT (Clinical Nutrition 2024, PMID 38309227).
compounds.effect_size_ci: Singapore older-adult RCT: favorable change in some PSQI components and reduced sleep latency at 4-8 wk, more evident in poor sleepers; raised serum serotonin. Modest, subjective, not PSG. No pooled CI for stand-alone insomnia.
compounds.clears_mcid: Unclear - subjective subscale changes; no PSG MCID demonstrated.
compounds.trial_dose: 100-300 mg/day (older-adult trial ~100 mg)
compounds.retail_dose: 50-100 mg - often at/below the lower trial dose
compounds.population_studied: Older adults (Singapore RCT), often poor sleepers; some combination-product trials (GABA+5-HTP).
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Weak; not shown in healthy younger adults as monotherapy.
compounds.funding_split: not reported
compounds.outlier_leverage: Sparse evidence base; the older-adult RCT carries most weight.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Historical: 5-HTP 'Peak-X' contaminant associated with EMS-like cases (1990s); theoretical serotonin-syndrome risk with serotonergic drugs. No current ban.
compounds.conditional_on: Signal conditional on being a poor sleeper / older adult.
compounds.verdict: Thin. No adequately powered stand-alone insomnia RCT; recent evidence is a modest older-adult trial helping poor sleepers on some PSQI components, plus combination products that confound the ingredient. Serotonin-load and historical Peak-X contamination concerns argue for caution. Not decision-grade for sleep.
primary_sources: Sutanto CN 2024, Clin Nutr, PMID 38309227 (5-HTP older adults, sleep & gut microbiota)
Byun JI 2018, J Clin Neurol (GABA/5-HTP combination - confounded)
NIH ODS / LiverTox 5-HTP entries; Peak-X/EMS historical literature

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Check 1 (funding-source subgroup) compounded by Check 5 (population transfer)
compounds.trial_count: Multiple double-blind RCTs (Kasper et al. 2010-2015) + network meta-analysis
compounds.total_n: 170 (restlessness/disturbed-sleep trial); 539 vs paroxetine/placebo (Kasper 2014); thousands pooled across program
compounds.largest_independent_trial: No large sponsor-independent Silexan trial identified.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Kasper 2014 GAD: HAMA reduction superior to placebo, comparable to paroxetine (HAMA -14.1 vs paroxetine -11.3 vs placebo -9.5). Sleep sub-scores and PSQI improved secondary to anxiolysis. Effect sizes moderate for anxiety; sleep effect derivative.
compounds.clears_mcid: For anxiety: YES (HAMA change clinically meaningful). For sleep as a primary endpoint: not established independent of anxiety.
compounds.trial_dose: 80 mg/day Silexan (single standardized capsule)
compounds.retail_dose: 80 mg Silexan (CalmAid/Lasea) - retail matches trial dose exactly
compounds.population_studied: GAD, subsyndromal/subthreshold anxiety, 'restlessness and disturbed sleep' out-patients (n=170) - anxious populations, not primary insomnia.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Limited transfer to a healthy, non-anxious poor sleeper.
compounds.funding_split: No independent-only pooled estimate; the Silexan program is overwhelmingly Dr. Willmar Schwabe-funded - the main caveat.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Consistent across several trials, not one-study-driven, but all from one sponsor.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Generally well tolerated (eructation/lavender belching main AE). No liver signal. Not FDA-approved as a drug; sold as a supplement in the US.
compounds.not_a_supplement: If the driver is an anxiety disorder, first-line care is CBT/SSRIs, not an OTC oil.
compounds.conditional_on: Benefit conditional on anxiety-related sleep disturbance; not demonstrated for non-anxious primary insomnia.
compounds.verdict: The best-evidenced botanical here - but it is an ANXIOLYTIC, and sleep improvement is downstream of anxiety relief, not a primary hypnotic action. Multiple RCTs (incl. vs paroxetine) show real HAMA reductions in GAD/subsyndromal anxiety; disturbed sleep improves as the anxiety lifts. Most trials are manufacturer-funded (Schwabe), which tempers confidence. Reasonable if the problem is anxiety-driven sleeplessness.
primary_sources: Kasper S 2014, Int J Neuropsychopharmacol, DOI 10.1017/S1461145714000017 (vs paroxetine & placebo)
Kasper S 2015, Eur Neuropsychopharmacol S0924977X15002424 (restlessness/disturbed sleep, n=170)
Yap WS 2019, Sci Rep, DOI 10.1038/s41598-019-54529-9 (network meta-analysis)

compounds.trial_count: Sutanto 2022 meta: 18 articles screened, 4 pooled; plus older Hartmann-era trials
compounds.total_n: Small pooled sample across 4 meta-analyzed RCTs
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Historical Hartmann/Schneider-Helmert 1 g trials (independent, academic).
compounds.effect_size_ci: Sutanto 2022: WASO shortened ~-81 min per gram (SMD -1.08; 95% CI -1.89 to -0.28; P=0.017). Dose-gated: >=1 g gave WASO 28.9 min vs 56.6 min for <1 g (P=0.001). No significant effect on other sleep components.
compounds.clears_mcid: YES for WASO at >=1 g (a ~28-min reduction is clinically meaningful) - but only that endpoint.
compounds.trial_dose: >=1 g at bedtime (older SOL work used 1-4 g)
compounds.retail_dose: 500 mg per capsule typical; many users take <1 g and fall below the effective threshold
compounds.population_studied: Mild insomnia and normal subjects with longer-than-average sleep latency; some clinical insomnia.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Transfers to healthy long-latency sleepers (studied population); little effect in good sleepers.
compounds.funding_split: not reported
compounds.outlier_leverage: Only 4 trials pooled - the WASO effect could shift with additional trials; treat CI with caution.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: 1989-90 EMS outbreak (Showa Denko contaminated batch, 'Peak-X'); FDA import restrictions lifted 2005; product now sold OTC. Caution with serotonergic drugs (serotonin syndrome).
compounds.conditional_on: Benefit conditional on >=1 g dose and on mild insomnia / long-latency sleepers.
compounds.verdict: A real but narrow effect: at >=1 g it reduces wake-after-sleep-onset, best in mild insomnia or long-latency normal sleepers. Modest and dose-gated. Carries a serious historical safety scar (1989 contaminated-batch eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome, >1500 cases, ~30+ deaths - a manufacturing contaminant, not the molecule). Buy only reputable, high-purity product at adequate dose.
primary_sources: Sutanto CN 2022, Nutr Rev, PMID 33942088 (DOI 10.1093/nutrit/nuab027; WASO -81 min/g)
Hartmann E 1974/1977 (L-tryptophan sleep latency, mild insomnia)
Belongia EA 1990, NEJM (EMS / L-tryptophan contamination)

products.servings_per_day_to_hit_trial_dose: 1 tablet = 1 g (meets the >=1 g bedtime threshold); 1-4 tablets covers the historic 1-4 g SOL range
products.certification: none (NOW is UL/NSF GMP-audited but not NSF Certified for Sport for this SKU)
products.note: Choosing the 1000 mg single-tablet SKU avoids the common failure mode where users take one 500 mg cap and fall below the 1 g effective dose. Take at bedtime. Search URL, not a fixed ASIN.

compounds.trial_count: Cochrane review for anxiety (Pittler & Ernst): ~12 RCTs; sleep-specific RCTs sparse
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Kava-anxiety Cochrane pooled analysis (Pittler & Ernst 2003).
compounds.effect_size_ci: Anxiety: significant HAMA reduction vs placebo (Cochrane weighted mean difference favoring kava). Sleep-specific outcome data are thin and secondary.
compounds.clears_mcid: For anxiety possibly; for sleep as a primary endpoint - not established.
compounds.trial_dose: Standardized to ~70-210 mg kavalactones/day in anxiety trials
compounds.retail_dose: Variable kavalactone content; often poorly standardized
compounds.population_studied: Generalized/situational anxiety adults (efficacy); sleep is not the primary studied endpoint.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Not a demonstrated hypnotic in healthy adults.
compounds.funding_split: not reported
compounds.outlier_leverage: not applicable - the decisive issue is safety, not efficacy leverage.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: FDA 2002 consumer advisory (severe liver injury); FDA 2023 memorandum concluding recreational/relaxation use 'not safe for human consumption'; historical bans/restrictions in Germany, UK, Switzerland, Australia; >100 suspected hepatotoxicity cases with transplants and deaths; NIH LiverTox monograph.
compounds.verdict: Recommend AGAINST for sleep. Efficacy evidence is for ANXIETY (Cochrane-level, kavain), not sleep per se, and it is overshadowed by a serious hepatotoxicity signal: FDA 2002 consumer advisory, temporary bans in Germany/UK/Switzerland, >100 suspected severe liver-injury cases including transplants and deaths. The risk-benefit for an OTC sleep aid is unacceptable.
primary_sources: Pittler MH & Ernst E 2003, Cochrane Database Syst Rev (kava for anxiety)
FDA 2002 Consumer Advisory on kava-containing supplements; FDA 2023 scientific memorandum (fda.gov/media/169556)
NIH LiverTox Kava, NBK548637

compounds.trial_count: 1-2 small RCTs + combination products
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Ngan & Conduit 2011, Phytother Res.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Ngan 2011: small but significant improvement in subjective sleep-quality diary rating vs placebo tea; no objective PSG effect. Underpowered.
compounds.clears_mcid: NO - subjective-only, small.
compounds.trial_dose: 2 g passionflower as tea
compounds.retail_dose: Capsule extracts of variable strength; often in multi-herb blends
compounds.population_studied: Healthy adults with mild sleep complaints (Ngan & Conduit 2011, n=41 tea crossover).
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Studied in healthy mild poor sleepers; signal weak.
compounds.funding_split: not reported
compounds.outlier_leverage: Single small study drives the claim.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: none found; generally well tolerated.
compounds.verdict: Thin. One small positive tea RCT and a few low-quality trials; frequently bundled with valerian, confounding attribution. Not decision-grade as a stand-alone sleep aid.

compounds.trial_count: ~40+ RCTs; two large IPD/aggregate meta-analyses
compounds.largest_independent_trial: VITAL (Manson/Martineau, NEJM 2019; respiratory analysis Thorax 2021), n=25,871, 2000 IU/day — no reduction in ARI
compounds.effect_size_ci: 2021 aggregate: OR 0.94 (0.88-1.00), p=0.057 — NULL. 2017 IPD overall OR 0.88 (0.81-0.96) but diluted to null once VIDARIS/ViDA/VITAL added. Deficiency subgroup (baseline <25 nmol/L) 2017 OR 0.30 (0.17-0.53). Dose-response trap: on bone, 4000-10000 IU LOWERED BMD vs 400 IU (Burt JAMA 2019) — more is not better.
compounds.clears_mcid: No in replete adults (null); yes only when correcting frank deficiency
compounds.trial_dose: Daily 400-4000 IU (10-100 mcg); daily/weekly dosing effective, single large bolus doses NOT effective
compounds.retail_dose: 1000-2000 IU (25-50 mcg) cholecalciferol daily — overlaps trial range
compounds.population_studied: Mixed: general adults, children, and deficient subgroups across ~40 RCTs. Benefit concentrated in profoundly deficient participants.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Poor — benefit is a deficiency-repletion effect, does not transfer to a replete healthy adult
compounds.funding_split: Largely government/independent-funded (VITAL, ViDA, VIDARIS); not a funding artifact
compounds.outlier_leverage: The 2017 'positive' pooled effect lost significance once later large independent trials were added — the signal hinged on smaller early trials
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No respiratory-specific advisory; hypercalcemia/toxicity at sustained high intake is the safety ceiling
compounds.not_a_supplement: For replete adults, sunlight/diet; deficiency is corrected with cheap generic D3, not an immune-branded product
compounds.conditional_on: Baseline 25(OH)D below ~25-30 nmol/L (frank deficiency), corrected with daily or weekly (not bolus) dosing
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for immunity if you are vitamin D replete. The one honest benefit is correcting genuine deficiency, which is cheap and does not require an 'immune' product. In replete adults the effect is null.

Martineau AR et al. BMJ 2017;356:i6583, PMID 28202713
VITAL respiratory analysis (Thorax 2021)
Burt LA et al. JAMA 2019;322:736 (bone dose-response), PMID 31454046
Jolliffe DA et al. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2024 stratified aggregate

products.servings_per_day_to_hit_trial_dose: 1 softgel/day, at the top of the ~1000-2000 IU repletion range

compounds.compound: Vitamin C (regular prophylaxis and cold treatment)
compounds.trial_count: ~29 incidence + 31 duration comparisons (Cochrane)
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Hemilä Cochrane pooled base (independent); no single sponsor drives it
compounds.effect_size_ci: Incidence general pop: RR ~0.97, no effect. Duration: -8% adults (95% CI 3-13%), -14% children (5-22%). Therapeutic dosing at onset: no consistent benefit. Extreme-stress subgroup incidence: RR 0.48 (0.35-0.64).
compounds.clears_mcid: No — 8% of a ~7-day cold is roughly half a day, below any meaningful threshold for a healthy adult
compounds.trial_dose: >=200 mg/day regular supplementation (many trials 1 g/day)
compounds.retail_dose: 500-1000 mg/day ascorbic acid — meets or exceeds trial dose
compounds.population_studied: General population (incidence/duration) and a distinct subgroup under extreme physical stress (marathon runners, skiers, soldiers)
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Duration effect is trivial; the halved-incidence effect does NOT transfer from marathoners to sedentary adults
compounds.funding_split: Not reported as a funding split; large independent Cochrane base
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not applicable — effect is small but consistent across many trials, not outlier-driven
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None found; GI upset and oxalate kidney-stone risk at gram doses
compounds.conditional_on: Incidence benefit applies only to short bouts of extreme physical/cold stress (marathons, sub-arctic exercise)
compounds.verdict: Do not buy to avoid catching colds — regular supplementation does not lower incidence in the general population. Daily supplementation shaves a modest, sub-clinical fraction off cold duration; taking it only after symptoms start does nothing. Genuine benefit exists ONLY for people under extreme acute physical stress.
primary_sources: Hemilä H, Chalker E. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2013;CD000980, PMID 23440782
Douglas RM et al. earlier Cochrane iterations

compounds.trial_count: 7 RCTs (Hemilä 2017 lozenge meta); 2024 Cochrane broader
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Hemilä 2017 pooled (independent reanalysis of Prasad, Petrus, Mossad et al.)
compounds.effect_size_ci: Cold duration -33% (95% CI 21-45%); acetate -40%, gluconate -28% (difference NS). No added benefit above ~100 mg/day. 2024 Cochrane (Nault) rated certainty low and was more equivocal; Hemilä published a formal rebuttal.
compounds.clears_mcid: Yes if formulation is right — roughly 2 fewer days of a 7-day cold clears the threshold
compounds.trial_dose: 80-207 mg/day ELEMENTAL zinc as acetate/gluconate lozenges, dissolved in mouth every ~2h, no chelating fillers (no citric/tartaric acid, mannitol/sorbitol)
compounds.retail_dose: Lozenges commonly 5-23 mg elemental per lozenge; most consumers take too few, or products bind zinc to citrate/aspartate or contain flavor acids that neutralize ionic zinc — delivering far less bioavailable ionic Zn2+ than trials
compounds.population_studied: Adults with naturally acquired common colds, treatment started within 24-48h
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Transfers to a healthy adult with an acute cold; does NOT support daily prophylactic capsules
compounds.funding_split: Hemilä's base is largely independent; 2024 Cochrane independent
compounds.outlier_leverage: Effect consistent across 7 trials, not outlier-dependent; the acetate/gluconate split is the main heterogeneity source
compounds.regulatory_advisory: FDA 2009 warning against INTRANASAL zinc gluconate (Zicam) — permanent anosmia. Applies to nasal gels/sprays, not oral lozenges.
compounds.conditional_on: Ionic zinc acetate/gluconate lozenge, ~75-100 mg/day elemental, started <24h, no citrate/mannitol/sorbitol chelators, dosed through the day
compounds.verdict: Conditional buy for TREATMENT only, and only a correctly formulated lozenge. High-dose ionic zinc acetate/gluconate lozenges started within 24h can meaningfully shorten a cold. Most retail products fail on formulation, not the headline mg. Prophylactic daily zinc does little or nothing for colds.
primary_sources: Hemilä H. JRSM Open 2017;8(5), PMID 28515951
Hemilä H et al. Open Forum Infect Dis 2017 IPD, PMID 28480298
Nault D et al. Cochrane 2024;CD014914, PMID 38719213

compounds.effect_size_ci: Prevention: post-hoc pooled RRR ~10-20%, not statistically significant, deemed of questionable clinical relevance. Treatment: only 2 of 6 duration trials significant; no consistent effect.

compounds.trial_count: ~23-24 RCTs (Cochrane 2022)
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Mixed; several independent daycare/school trials contribute alongside sponsor trials
compounds.effect_size_ci: At least one URTI episode: RR ~0.76 (0.65-0.89). Episode rate ratio 0.79 (0.71-0.89), p<0.001. Also reduced antibiotic use and school absence. GRADE low-to-moderate.
compounds.clears_mcid: Borderline/modest — meaningful at population level (fewer episodes, less antibiotic use) but individual effect is small
compounds.trial_dose: Strain-specific, typically 1e9-1e10 CFU/day (e.g., L. rhamnosus GG, L. casei Shirota/DN-114001, B. animalis)
compounds.retail_dose: CFU and strain vary enormously; many products do not use the studied strains or guarantee viable CFU to end of shelf life
compounds.population_studied: General adults and children (community, daycare, some athletes)
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Reasonably — trials include healthy community populations
compounds.funding_split: Many trials manufacturer-funded (Yakult, Danone, Chr. Hansen); pooled effect persists but certainty is downgraded partly for this
compounds.outlier_leverage: High heterogeneity; effect not reliant on a single study but strain mix matters
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No general advisory; caution/sepsis risk in immunocompromised and critically ill — not for that population
compounds.conditional_on: Use a specifically studied strain at studied CFU; benefit is strain-dependent, not a class effect
compounds.verdict: Conditional and modest. Cochrane finds probiotics reduce the number of people getting at least one URTI and cut episode rates, but certainty is low-to-moderate, effects are strain-specific, heterogeneity is high, and many trials are industry-funded. A reasonable but not compelling buy, and only specific strains.
primary_sources: Zhao Y et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2022;CD006895.pub4, PMID 36001877

Josling P. Adv Ther 2001;18:189, PMID 11697022

compounds.clears_mcid: No — overall null; subgroup effect is exploratory
compounds.trial_dose: 1000 mg/day (the dose with the subgroup signal); 500 mg/day also tested
compounds.retail_dose: Typically 500 mg/day — below the 1000 mg dose that produced the subgroup effect
compounds.population_studied: Community adults 18-85; positive signal only in post-hoc subgroup (age >=40, self-rated fit)

compounds.outlier_leverage: Effect exists only in a carved-out subgroup, not the main analysis
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None found
compounds.conditional_on: Only the exploratory subgroup (physically fit adults >=40 at 1000 mg/day) showed anything

compounds.trial_count: 1 relevant flu-symptom RCT; separate solid COPD RCT base
compounds.largest_independent_trial: De Flora S et al. 1997, n=262 (multicenter Italian, independent)
compounds.effect_size_ci: De Flora 1997: seroconversion to A/H1N1 unchanged (NAC did not prevent infection), but only 25% of infected NAC subjects became symptomatic vs 79% on placebo; fewer/less severe influenza-like episodes. Single-trial, not replicated for this endpoint.
compounds.clears_mcid: Plausibly in the studied elderly/comorbid group; unproven and untransferred to healthy adults
compounds.trial_dose: 600 mg twice daily (1200 mg/day) for 6 months
compounds.retail_dose: 600-1200 mg/day capsules — matches trial
compounds.population_studied: Elderly (78% >=65y), 62% with chronic disease (De Flora 1997) — NOT healthy adults
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Not demonstrated — the trial population was old and comorbid
compounds.funding_split: Not a funding artifact; the issue is single-trial, narrow population
compounds.outlier_leverage: The immunity claim rests on one trial
compounds.regulatory_advisory: FDA (2022) holds NAC is EXCLUDED from the dietary-supplement definition (approved as a drug first); currently sold only under FDA enforcement discretion. Regulatory status, not efficacy, is the flag.
compounds.not_a_supplement: NAC's robust evidence is as a DRUG: mucolytic reducing COPD exacerbations (BRONCUS, PANTHEON/HIACE) and the standard antidote for acetaminophen overdose — not a general immune booster
compounds.conditional_on: Elderly or chronically ill population; general antioxidant/mucolytic use, not cold prophylaxis in the healthy
compounds.verdict: Do not buy as a general immune supplement. Its real, drug-grade evidence is as a mucolytic that reduces COPD exacerbations and as the paracetamol-overdose antidote. The single positive flu-symptom trial is old, in elderly/comorbid patients, and unreplicated; it did not prevent infection, only symptomatic expression.
primary_sources: De Flora S et al. Eur Respir J 1997;10:1535, PMID 9230243
FDA Final Guidance on NAC enforcement discretion, Aug 2022

compounds.trial_count: ~33 RCTs (Hu 2017 meta), quality mixed; many Chinese-language, some industry (KalmCold/Kan Jang)
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Hu 2017 pooled base; Coon & Ernst 2004 earlier systematic review
compounds.effect_size_ci: Hu 2017: improved cough and sore throat and shortened symptom course vs placebo/usual care; effect real but heterogeneity high and several trials low quality / combination products confound the single-agent claim
compounds.clears_mcid: Plausibly for symptom relief, but confounded by combination formulas and trial quality
compounds.trial_dose: ~60-200 mg/day andrographolides (standardized extracts SHA-10/KalmCold)
compounds.retail_dose: Extracts standardized to andrographolides, typically in the trial range
compounds.population_studied: Adults and children with acute respiratory tract infections; many trials use fixed combos (Kan Jang = andrographis + eleuthero)
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Applies to acutely ill patients; not a prophylactic for the healthy
compounds.funding_split: Positive trials include manufacturer products (Swedish Herbal Institute Kan Jang, KalmCold); independent low-quality trials also positive but heterogeneous
compounds.outlier_leverage: Heterogeneity and combination-product confounding rather than a single outlier
compounds.regulatory_advisory: STRONG: Australian TGA — 287 anaphylaxis reports to 31 Dec 2025 including a 2024 fatality; mandatory allergy warning since 2019; TGA has proposed REMOVING andrographis from permitted ingredients. This is the deciding factor.
compounds.conditional_on: Symptomatic relief of an active ARTI, not prevention
compounds.verdict: Efficacy is the strongest of the herbals here — meta-analysis shows genuine improvement in cough and sore throat versus placebo — but a serious, active regulatory safety signal caps this. Not a recommended buy: the anaphylaxis risk outweighs a symptom-relief benefit you can get more safely.
primary_sources: Hu XY et al. PLoS One 2017;12:e0181780, PMID 28783758 (+2018 correction)
Coon JT, Ernst E. Planta Med 2004;70:293, PMID 15095142
TGA safety advisory, Andrographis and anaphylaxis, updated 2024-2025

compounds.clears_mcid: Uncertain — nominal reductions are meaningful for athletes but precision is low

compounds.retail_dose: Typically 2-10 g/day capsules or scoops — well below trial doses
compounds.population_studied: Endurance/exercise-trained adults under training load (not sedentary healthy adults)

compounds.regulatory_advisory: None specific; caution with dairy allergy

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Outlier/quality leverage (check 2)
compounds.trial_count: 10 RCTs in the 2022 pooled meta-analysis (Black/Ford), n=1030; plus the independent Weerts 2020 RCT (n=190).
compounds.total_n: ~1220 across positive pooled trials + largest independent trial
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Weerts et al. 2020, Gastroenterology (n=190/analyzed ~178): small-intestinal- and ileocolonic-release peppermint oil vs placebo, NO significant benefit on co-primary abdominal pain response or global relief at 8 weeks; only secondary pain-severity outcomes improved.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Global symptoms not improving RR 0.65 (95% CI 0.43-0.98), NNT=4; abdominal pain not improving RR 0.76 (95% CI 0.62-0.93), NNT=7 (Black 2022 meta-analysis, Aliment Pharmacol Ther).
compounds.clears_mcid: Yes on pooled dichotomous responder outcomes (NNT 4-7 is clinically meaningful) — but the largest trial failed the FDA-standard primary endpoint.
compounds.trial_dose: 180-225 mg enteric/gastro-resistant peppermint oil (~0.2 mL) 2-3x/day = 360-540 mg/day
compounds.retail_dose: ~180-225 mg peppermint oil per enteric-coated capsule, 1-2 caps 2-3x/day (matches trial range)
compounds.population_studied: Adults with IBS (Rome II-IV), mixed subtypes; most trials 2-4 weeks, few high-quality.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No. Benefit is in symptomatic IBS; no rationale in a healthy adult.
compounds.funding_split: Not cleanly split in the meta-analysis, but many older positive trials were small/industry-linked; the independent, government/academic-funded Weerts 2020 trial (4 Dutch hospitals) was null on both co-primary endpoints (abdominal pain response and global relief at 8 weeks).
compounds.outlier_leverage: Yes — pooled positivity leans on small, short, older trials with likely unblinding (menthol taste/smell); the single best-powered independent trial (Weerts 2020, Gastroenterology 158:123-136) removed the primary-endpoint effect.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None material for efficacy; label caution re GERD/heartburn aggravation with non-enteric formulations. No TGA/EMA/FDA safety advisory found.
compounds.conditional_on: IBS with abdominal pain/spasm; use enteric or ileocolonic-release formulation to limit reflux/heartburn.
compounds.verdict: Conditional buy for IBS abdominal pain/global symptoms — the best OTC option in this category, but the effect is fragile: it holds in pooled older trials yet the largest independent trial missed its primary endpoint. Reasonable to trial for 4 weeks; stop if no benefit.
primary_sources: Black CJ, et al. Aliment Pharmacol Ther 2022 (10-RCT meta-analysis, NNT 4/7)
Weerts ZZRM, et al. Gastroenterology 2020;158:123-136 (independent RCT, null primary endpoint) PMID 32289372
Alammar N, et al. BMC Complement Altern Med 2019;19:21 (pooled RR 2.39 global improvement) PMID 30654773
Ford AC, et al. ACG monograph / IBS guideline conditional recommendation

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Check 4 — dose in trials (10-20 g/day) vs retail single serving (~3.4 g); the only refutation with teeth, but mitigable by titration
compounds.trial_count: Soluble-fiber IBS meta-analysis (Moayyedi/Ford 2014, 7 psyllium RCTs); constipation meta-analysis (van der Schoot, AJCN 2024) and elderly meta-analysis (Foods 2025).
compounds.total_n: ~500 in soluble-fiber IBS pooling; several hundred more across constipation RCTs
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Bijkerk et al. 2009, BMJ (n=275, primary care): psyllium 10 g/day significantly improved IBS symptom severity vs placebo and bran at 3 months.
compounds.effect_size_ci: IBS: symptoms not improving RR 0.83 (95% CI 0.73-0.94), NNT≈7 (Ford/Moayyedi 2014, BMJ). Constipation: significant increase in stool frequency and improved consistency (AJCN 2024 meta-analysis; ~66% responders vs ~41% control).
compounds.clears_mcid: Yes — modest but clinically usable; effect largest in IBS-C and constipation.
compounds.trial_dose: ≥10 g/day psyllium for ≥4 weeks (optimal); IBS trials commonly 10-20 g/day
compounds.retail_dose: ~3.4-5 g psyllium per single serving (e.g. Metamucil rounded tsp ~3.4 g) — most users take one serving, under the ≥10 g/day trial target
compounds.population_studied: Adults with IBS (all subtypes, best in IBS-C) and adults/elderly with chronic idiopathic constipation.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Partial — a healthy adult with adequate fiber gets little symptom benefit; benefit is in constipation/IBS or low-fiber diets.
compounds.funding_split: Not a decisive issue; positive results appear in independent/academic pooled analyses (Cochrane-grade fiber reviews).
compounds.outlier_leverage: No single-study dependence; effect is consistent across the soluble-fiber pool (contrast: insoluble bran shows no benefit and can worsen symptoms).
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None. Well-established safety; caution only re esophageal/bowel obstruction if taken with insufficient fluid.
compounds.conditional_on: Take with adequate water; benefit strongest in IBS-C/constipation, weaker in IBS-D pain.
compounds.verdict: Buy — the strongest evidence in the category. Cheap, independent, guideline-endorsed soluble/gel-forming fiber for IBS global symptoms and for chronic constipation. Titrate to an effective dose and give it 4 weeks.
primary_sources: Moayyedi P, Ford AC, et al. Am J Gastroenterol 2014 / BMJ soluble fiber meta-analysis (RR 0.83)
Bijkerk CJ, et al. BMJ 2009;339:b3154 (independent primary-care RCT) PMID 19713235
van der Schoot A, et al. Am J Clin Nutr 2024 (fiber for chronic constipation meta-analysis)
Foods 2025;14:2315 (fiber for constipation in elderly meta-analysis)

compounds.trial_count: AAD: ~21 RCTs (Szajewska/Kołodziej 2015 meta-analysis); pediatric acute diarrhea: 6+ RCTs.
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Pooled Szajewska & Kołodziej 2015 (Aliment Pharmacol Ther) across ~21 RCTs; consistent 50%+ relative risk reduction.

compounds.clears_mcid: Yes for AAD and acute pediatric diarrhea (NNT≈10; ~1 day shorter illness).

compounds.retail_dose: 250-500 mg (~5-10 billion CFU) per capsule — matches trial dosing
compounds.population_studied: Adults and children on antibiotics (AAD prevention) and children with acute gastroenteritis; NOT healthy adults seeking general gut benefits.

compounds.verdict: Conditional buy — genuinely effective for a specific job (preventing antibiotic-associated diarrhea, shortening acute infectious diarrhea), NOT for routine 'gut health.' Independent evidence, meaningful NNT. Avoid in the critically ill.
primary_sources: Szajewska H, Kołodziej M. Aliment Pharmacol Ther 2015 (AAD meta-analysis, RR 0.47)
McFarland LV. World J Gastroenterol 2010 (S. boulardii meta-analysis)
EMA 2018 referral/PRAC restriction on S. boulardii medicinal products (ICU/CVC contraindication)
Rannikko J, et al. Emerg Infect Dis 2021;27(8) (fungemia case series)

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Outlier leverage / funding-quality collapse (checks 1-2), reinforced by population transfer (check 5)
compounds.trial_count: Acute diarrhea: many small older RCTs + 2 large 2018 independent nulls; AAD: pooled with other Lactobacillus.
compounds.total_n: ~1800 in the two large independent gastroenteritis trials alone
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Schnadower D, et al. NEJM 2018;379:2002-2014 (n=943, 10 US pediatric EDs, NIH-funded): LGG 10^10 CFU BID = NO benefit over placebo for acute gastroenteritis.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Schnadower 2018 NEJM (n=943): NO benefit — moderate/severe disease in 11.8% LGG vs 12.6% placebo (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.68-1.35). Freedman 2018 (PROBIOTIC, n=886) also null. Older meta-analyses claimed ~-1 day duration but on low-quality evidence.
compounds.clears_mcid: No — the high-quality independent trials show no clinically meaningful effect on acute gastroenteritis.
compounds.trial_dose: 1×10^10 CFU BID (2×10^10 CFU/day)
compounds.retail_dose: 10-20 billion CFU/day (matches trial dose)
compounds.population_studied: Children with acute gastroenteritis (trials); some AAD-prevention data in children and adults. Adult IBS/general use largely untested.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No. No credible healthy-adult gut-health outcome data.

compounds.clears_mcid: Uncertain — statistical signal, but low certainty and heterogeneity make clinical significance unreliable.

compounds.funding_split: Substantial manufacturer funding across the positive literature; independent replication is inconsistent.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Yes — pooled effects are driven by specific products/strains and are heterogeneous; not a robust general effect.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Probiotic bacteremia/fungemia risk in critically ill/immunocompromised (general caution). No efficacy endorsement from ACG/AGA for IBS.

compounds.verdict: Do not buy as a class for IBS or 'gut health.' Meta-analyses show a signal but at low/very-low GRADE certainty with heavy heterogeneity and industry funding; ACG and AGA recommend against routine use outside a trial. Any benefit is strain-and-product-specific, not a class effect.

compounds.total_n: Small (tens to low hundreds per targeted trial)

compounds.verdict: Do not buy generic 'digestive enzyme' blends for IBS/gut health. The only justified uses are enzyme REPLACEMENT for a specific deficiency — lactase for lactose intolerance, and prescription PERT for pancreatic insufficiency, which is not an OTC supplement.

Hillilä M, et al. 2016 (alpha-galactosidase RCT)
AGA/ACG guidance on PERT for exocrine pancreatic insufficiency

compounds.trial_count: Several small-to-moderate Japanese RCTs (ulcer healing) + tiny permeability crossover + small UC enema pilot.
compounds.total_n: ~250 in the largest ulcer RCT; n=10 in the key permeability study
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Mahmood A, et al. Gut 2007 (n=10 crossover): zinc-carnosine 37.5 mg BID prevented indomethacin-induced increase in small-intestinal permeability and stimulated repair. Ulcer efficacy from larger Japanese RCTs.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Gastric ulcer: endoscopic improvement ~60% and higher symptom response vs comparator in an ~258-patient RCT. Permeability: prevented the ~3-fold indomethacin-induced rise in gut permeability in healthy volunteers (Mahmood 2007, n=10 crossover).
compounds.clears_mcid: Plausibly for ulcer healing as adjunct; unproven for functional gut symptoms/IBS.
compounds.trial_dose: 75 mg/day polaprezinc (37.5 mg BID; delivers ~16 mg elemental zinc) for gut integrity; up to 150 mg/day in ulcer trials
compounds.retail_dose: ~75 mg zinc-carnosine chelate (~16 mg elemental zinc) per typical supplement dose — matches the permeability-trial dose
compounds.population_studied: Gastric ulcer patients (adjunct to standard therapy); healthy volunteers given indomethacin; small UC enema pilots — largely Japanese cohorts.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Marginal — the permeability data are in an experimental NSAID-injury model, not everyday healthy-gut benefit.
compounds.funding_split: Older Japanese trials, some manufacturer involvement; limited independent Western replication.
compounds.outlier_leverage: The permeability claim rests on one n=10 study — thin.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Approved as a gastric drug (polaprezinc) in Japan; not an approved therapeutic elsewhere. No major safety advisory; watch cumulative zinc intake (copper depletion) with chronic use.
compounds.conditional_on: Gastric ulcer (adjunct to PPI/eradication) or NSAID-associated mucosal injury; not validated for IBS or general 'gut lining' claims.
compounds.verdict: Weak/conditional. Real but small-trial evidence for gastric mucosal protection and ulcer healing (mostly Japanese, adjunct to PPI) and one tiny crossover showing it blunts NSAID-induced gut permeability. Not established for 'leaky gut' or IBS. Mechanism ahead of outcomes.
primary_sources: Mahmood A, et al. Gut 2007;56:168-175 PMID 16777920 (permeability crossover)
Polaprezinc gastric ulcer multicenter RCT (2022, positive-controlled)
Polaprezinc enema in ulcerative colitis, pilot PMID 24286534

Jackman 2017 Front Physiol 8:390 (PMID 28638350)

compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No - benefit does not transfer to healthy trained adults; the meaningful signal is confined to catabolic/elderly populations.

compounds.regulatory_advisory: None found.

compounds.trial_count: ~40 RCTs (Saunders 2017 meta).

compounds.clears_mcid: Yes for high-intensity endurance/repeated-effort tasks; no for maximal strength.

compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Yes for the 1-4 min high-intensity domain; does NOT meaningfully transfer to pure 1RM strength or muscle growth.
compounds.funding_split: Not decisive; mechanism (carnosine buffering) is well established across independent labs.
compounds.outlier_leverage: No - distributed effect across many studies.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None found beyond benign paraesthesia (harmless tingling) at bolus doses.
compounds.conditional_on: Task is high-intensity and buffering-limited (~1-4 min); irrelevant for powerlifting-style maximal strength.
compounds.verdict: Buy only for its real domain: high-intensity efforts lasting ~1-4 minutes (repeated sprints, rowing, CrossFit-style work). It is NOT a maximal-strength or hypertrophy aid - marketing overreaches on that.

Hill 2007 Amino Acids 32:225 (PMID 16868650)

compounds.trial_count: 8-12 small RCTs.
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Varvik 2021 pooled analysis is the best synthesis; no single large independent confirmatory trial exists.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Vialpando/Varvik 2021 meta (8 studies, n=137): +6.4% reps to failure, SMD 0.196 (small); subgroups non-significant and authors concluded evidence does not support a recommendation. Trujillo-Colmena/three-level metas confirm SMD ~0.2 (95% CI ~0.01-0.39), fragile.
compounds.clears_mcid: No - a fraction of a rep advantage that does not reliably exceed noise.
compounds.trial_dose: 6-8 g citrulline malate (~3.5-4.5 g L-citrulline), 40-60 min pre-exercise.
compounds.retail_dose: 6-8 g standalone is on-dose, but many pre-workout blends contain only 1-3 g - below trial dose.
compounds.population_studied: Mostly young resistance-trained men, acute pre-exercise dosing.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Weakly - even in the studied healthy trained population the effect is small and unreliable.
compounds.funding_split: Several trials industry-adjacent; base too small to split cleanly.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Yes - pooled significance is fragile and hinges on a few small positive studies; CI lower bound near zero.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None found.
compounds.verdict: Borderline / skip. The vasodilator pump is real, but the performance benefit is small, inconsistent, and the meta-analysis authors themselves declined to recommend it. Effect sits near the null.

Trujillo-Colmena 2025 three-level meta, Nutrients 18:1881

compounds.trial_count: ~6-10 small RCTs.
compounds.total_n: Low hundreds pooled; individual trials n~20-30.
compounds.largest_independent_trial: No decisive large independent RCT; base is small early-phase studies.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Pooled maximal strength SMD 0.47 (95% CI 0.04-0.89); lower-body SMD 0.49 (95% CI 0.01-0.98) - both lower bounds essentially at zero. No effect on upper-body strength, power, or endurance. Ashtary-Larky 2022: no body-composition effect.
compounds.clears_mcid: Borderline - point estimate is moderate but the near-zero CI bound means the true effect may be trivial.
compounds.trial_dose: 2.5 g/day for 1+ weeks.
compounds.retail_dose: ~2.5 g/day - matches trial dose.
compounds.population_studied: Young resistance-trained men, short (1-6 week) trials.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Uncertain - the studied population is healthy trainees, but the effect is too fragile to bank on.
compounds.funding_split: Not formally split, but betaine is manufactured by ingredient suppliers (e.g. DuPont/Danisco) and several trials are industry-adjacent - contributes to the low confidence.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Yes - with CI lower bounds at 0.01-0.04, removing one small positive trial would likely null the result.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: None found for muscle dosing.
compounds.verdict: Skip pending better data. A borderline-significant strength signal exists but rests on small trials with a confidence interval nearly touching zero, and there is no body-composition benefit.
