Ashtary-Larky 2022 body-composition meta, Br J Nutr (PMID via Cambridge Core, failed body-comp)

compounds.trial_count: Dozens of RCTs; multiple metas.
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Burt 2019 (Calgary, JAMA 322:736, n=311) - independent: 4000 and 10000 IU/day LOWERED radial/tibial bone density vs 400 IU, demonstrating the wrong-direction dose-response and repletion harm.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Deficient (<25 nmol/L): large effect on hip/proximal strength; athletes <75 nmol/L: small strength effect (2023 Frontiers meta, 11 RCTs, n=436). Replete: no grip-strength effect. Falls reduced by active analogues in elderly.
compounds.clears_mcid: Yes in deficiency (proximal weakness reversal, fall reduction); no in repletion.
compounds.trial_dose: Repletion dosing ~1000-2000 IU/day (or equivalent) to restore normal 25(OH)D.
compounds.retail_dose: 1000-2000 IU adequate; 5000-10000 IU products are unnecessary and enter the harm range.
compounds.population_studied: Deficient/older adults (25(OH)D <25-50 nmol/L) and athletes with low baseline; distinct from replete healthy adults.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No - benefit does NOT transfer to a vitamin-D-replete healthy adult; grip strength unaffected when 25(OH)D >25 nmol/L.
compounds.funding_split: Not a decisive industry issue - largely publicly funded.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not applicable to the deficiency-repletion signal.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: High-dose harm signal: Burt 2019 JAMA bone-density decline; hypercalcaemia/toxicity above ~4000 IU/day chronic. Supports capping, not maximizing, the dose.
compounds.not_a_supplement: For a replete adult: nothing needed - sensible sun exposure/diet maintains status; extra vitamin D adds no strength.
compounds.conditional_on: Measured 25(OH)D below ~50 nmol/L (deficient/insufficient). Test before supplementing; do not exceed ~2000-4000 IU/day.
compounds.verdict: Conditional buy - correct a measured deficiency, then stop. Real strength/fall benefit only in deficient people; null in the already-replete, and high doses actively harm. This is a repletion story, not an ergogenic one.
primary_sources: 2023 athletes meta, Front Nutr 10:1163313 (PMID 37841405)
Beaudart 2014 muscle-strength meta, J Clin Endocrinol Metab (PMID 25162434)

compounds.verify_decisive_check: Check 1 — funding-source independence: every strength trial traces to the KSM-66 maker (Ixoreal) or industry-tied authors; no adequately powered independent replication exists.
compounds.trial_count: A few small single-site RCTs, predominantly manufacturer-funded.
compounds.largest_independent_trial: No adequately powered independent strength RCT exists; the evidence base is sponsor-dependent.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Wankhede 2015: bench-press 1RM +46 kg vs +26 kg placebo and large testosterone/muscle-size gains - effect sizes implausibly large for 8 weeks and unreplicated independently.
compounds.clears_mcid: Nominally yes in the sponsor trial, but the result is not trustworthy enough to credit.
compounds.trial_dose: 300 mg root extract twice daily (KSM-66), or ~600 mg/day standardized extract.
compounds.retail_dose: 600 mg KSM-66 - matches trial dose (dose is not the issue; credibility and safety are).
compounds.population_studied: Young men with little resistance-training experience (Wankhede 2015, n=57); small single-site trials.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Not credibly - the untrained-novice gains are confounded by learning effects and sponsor bias; no robust healthy-adult replication.
compounds.funding_split: Decisive. Positive strength trials trace to KSM-66 maker Ixoreal Biomed / extract suppliers; independent replication absent. This is why the grade is capped at 2.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Yes - the category's strength claim rests almost entirely on the Wankhede 2015 outlier.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Substantial. Denmark banned ashwagandha in food/supplements (2023, liver/thyroid/reproductive concerns); Iceland issued a liver-injury warning (2023); EU Heads of Food Safety Agencies prioritized it for an Article 8 procedure (June 2024); Bjornsson 2020 Iceland/US DILIN case series and NIH LiverTox document hepatotoxicity with 2-12 week latency.
compounds.not_a_supplement: Progressive resistance training plus adequate protein and sleep - the actual drivers of the outcomes attributed to ashwagandha.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for muscle/strength. The headline strength gains come from extract-manufacturer-funded trials with implausibly large effects and no independent replication - and multiple regulators have now flagged liver, thyroid and reproductive safety.
primary_sources: Wankhede 2015, J Int Soc Sports Nutr 12:43 (PMID 26609282) - industry-funded
Bjornsson 2020 liver-injury case series, Liver Int (PMID 31879990)
NIH LiverTox NBK548536
EU HoA Article 8 prioritization 2024; Danish/Icelandic advisories 2023

compounds.trial_count: ~20 RCTs in the primary meta; corroborated by an umbrella meta-of-metas (2024).
compounds.total_n: Hundreds pooled across strength and power outcomes.
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Many independent university crossover RCTs; effect is robust to any single study's removal.

compounds.trial_dose: 3-6 mg/kg ~60 min pre-exercise (jump benefit seen from ~1-2 mg/kg).
compounds.retail_dose: Pre-workouts/tablets 150-300 mg (~2-4 mg/kg for an 80 kg adult) - within the effective range.
compounds.population_studied: Trained and untrained adults, acute pre-exercise dosing; strength and power tasks.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Yes - demonstrated directly in healthy adults; effect is acute and reproducible.
compounds.funding_split: Not decisive - caffeine is generic and the literature is heavily independent/academic.
compounds.outlier_leverage: No - consistent small effect across many studies.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: General: keep total intake below ~400 mg/day (FDA/EFSA); WADA monitors but does not ban. No muscle-specific advisory.
compounds.verdict: Buy as an acute ergogenic. One of the few genuinely proven performance aids - small but real, independently replicated strength/power effect. Cheap, generic, well-characterized.

Grgic 2020 meta-of-metas, Sports Med (PMID 32488520)

compounds.compound: Testosterone boosters (Tribulus, D-aspartic acid, fenugreek blends)
compounds.trial_count: A handful of small RCTs, predominantly null.
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Melville 2015 (independent, D-aspartic acid, n=24) - no benefit, higher dose counterproductive.
compounds.effect_size_ci: D-aspartic acid: Melville 2015 RCT (n=24) - no rise in testosterone, 6 g/day trended DOWN. Tribulus: Rogerson 2007 and others - no testosterone or performance effect. Pooled: null.
compounds.clears_mcid: No - no effect to clear it.
compounds.trial_dose: Varies (e.g. D-aspartic acid 3-6 g/day; Tribulus ~750 mg/day).
compounds.retail_dose: Proprietary blends, frequently underdosed and undisclosed.
compounds.population_studied: Mostly young men; a few small RCTs, largely null.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: No benefit to transfer - null in the healthy men studied.
compounds.funding_split: Positive noise is industry/anecdotal; controlled independent trials are null.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Not applicable - no robust positive pool to leverage.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: Sporadic contamination/adulteration warnings for proprietary 'test booster' blends (undeclared steroids/DMAA-type stimulants) from FDA.

Rogerson 2007 Tribulus RCT, J Strength Cond Res 21:348 (PMID 17530942)

compounds.trial_count: ~10-12 RCTs (n~437-513 pooled)
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Igarashi et al. 2024 (250 mg, older adults, ~n80) among larger; independent adequately powered outcome trials remain scarce.
compounds.effect_size_ci: NAD+ rises robustly (SMD large, p<0.001). Physical performance: pooled effect non-significant. Igarashi 2024 (250 mg, older adults) shorter 4 m gait; Yi 2022 improved 6-min walk. Glucose/lipid meta-analysis (12 RCTs, n=513): NAD up, but HbA1c, fasting glucose, lipids not significantly changed vs placebo.
compounds.clears_mcid: no - performance changes are small and inconsistent; pooled physical-performance effect does not reach significance, let alone MCID.
compounds.retail_dose: 250-1000 mg/day (retail matches trial range)
compounds.population_studied: Healthy middle-aged (avg ~58y) and older adults; several trials in amateur athletes and Asian cohorts.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Weak. Signals appear in older/at-risk or athlete cohorts; no durable functional benefit demonstrated in healthy adults.
compounds.funding_split: No formal funding-subgroup meta-analysis exists; the more positive trials cluster among manufacturer-linked / single-region groups. Independent large-outcome data are thin.
compounds.outlier_leverage: Positive pooled signals lean on a few small trials; removing them collapses the effect toward null.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: FDA drug-preclusion saga: FDA told marketers in 2022 NMN is excluded from the dietary-supplement definition (prior drug-investigation clause); after NPA litigation FDA reversed and declared NMN lawful in supplements (2025). Legal status, not a safety advisory. No TGA/EMA safety signal.
compounds.conditional_on: Any plausible benefit is limited to older adults with declining function, not healthy midlife users.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for healthspan/longevity. NMN reliably raises blood NAD+, but that is a biomarker, not an outcome. The largest, most rigorous syntheses show physical-function and metabolic benefits are non-significant; the scattered positive trials are small, short, and largely industry- or single-region (China/Japan) sourced.

Cureus 2024 systematic review PMC11365583 (10 RCTs, physical performance non-significant)
Crit Rev Food Sci Nutr 2024, PMID 39116016 (glucose/lipid meta-analysis, 12 RCTs n=513)
PMC11557618 (glucose/lipid meta-analysis)
Yi et al. 2022 (6-min walk, healthy adults)

compounds.trial_count: Multiple RCTs incl. independent (Martens 2018; NCT03821623; NR-SAFE 2023)
compounds.total_n: Dozens per trial (Martens n=24 crossover; NCT03821623 larger)
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Martens et al. 2018, Nat Commun (n=24 crossover, healthy 55-79y): NAD+ up, BP/stiffness endpoints exploratory and non-significant.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Martens 2018 (Nat Commun, independent, U. Colorado): 1000 mg/d x6 wk raised NAD+ ~60%; systolic BP fell ~9 mmHg in the elevated-BP subgroup but NOT statistically significant in the full cohort. Follow-up NCT03821623 (Frontiers Cardiovasc Med 2022) found NR did not significantly reduce systolic BP or aortic stiffness (primary endpoints null).
compounds.clears_mcid: no - the ~9 mmHg BP signal would be clinically meaningful IF real, but it did not reach significance; confirmatory trial was null.
compounds.trial_dose: 500-1000 mg/day (safety up to 3000 mg/day)
compounds.retail_dose: 250-500 mg/day (typically below the 1000 mg trial dose)
compounds.population_studied: Healthy midlife/older adults (Martens, Boulder); Parkinson's (NR-SAFE); overweight adults; hypertensive older adults.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: NAD+ elevation transfers to healthy adults; functional/vascular benefit does not.
compounds.funding_split: Much NR work is ChromaDex (Niagen)-funded; the key BP trials (Seals/Martens lab) are comparatively independent and were essentially null - so the null is not a funding artifact.
compounds.outlier_leverage: The apparent BP benefit hinges on one subgroup in one small trial; not replicated.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No regulator advisory. Preclinical caution: a 2023 mouse study reported NR promoted metastasis of aggressive tumours in immunocompromised mice (triple-negative breast); species/immune-status dependent, not established in humans - relevant caution for active-cancer patients.
compounds.conditional_on: Any BP interest is confined to people with above-normal systolic BP, not normotensive healthy adults.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy for longevity. Best-characterised NAD precursor with genuine independent RCTs and a clean safety record - but the flagship blood-pressure/vascular endpoints were non-significant in the primary analyses. NAD+ goes up; hard outcomes do not.

Frontiers Cardiovasc Med 2022, PMID 35620522 / NCT03821623 (BP & stiffness null)
NR-SAFE, Nat Commun 2023 (3000 mg safety in Parkinson's)
Conze/ChromaDex NIAGEN safety RCT PMC6611812

compounds.trial_count: Dozens of RCTs; multiple meta-analyses
compounds.largest_independent_trial: Multiple; e.g., lipid dose-response meta-analysis PMC9506025 - mixed/modest. No landmark independent trial shows a meaningful healthspan benefit.
compounds.effect_size_ci: Lipids: meta-analyses show small reductions in total-C/TG/LDL in some pools, null in others; HDL unchanged. Vascular/endothelial outcomes inconsistent and dose-unrelated. Anthropometric/metabolic outcomes in obesity: no significant clinical improvement. CRP/TNF-alpha modestly reduced in CVD patients; IL-6 unchanged.
compounds.clears_mcid: no - where significant, effect sizes are small and clinically marginal; heterogeneity high.
compounds.trial_dose: 150 mg - 1000+ mg/day (some to 5 g)
compounds.retail_dose: 250-500 mg/day (trans-resveratrol)
compounds.population_studied: Broad: T2D, obesity/overweight, CVD, cognition, healthy adults.
compounds.transfer_to_healthy: Poor. Signals concentrate in diseased/dysmetabolic cohorts; may be counterproductive in healthy exercisers (Gliemann 2013: resveratrol blunted training-induced cardiovascular benefit in older men).
compounds.funding_split: Not consistently split; heterogeneity and bioavailability are the dominant problems, not a single funding artifact.
compounds.outlier_leverage: High heterogeneity; several pooled signals are fragile to study exclusion.
compounds.regulatory_advisory: No major efficacy advisory; GI intolerance at high doses; potential CYP interaction. Note the exercise-blunting signal as a functional downside.
compounds.conditional_on: Any metabolic benefit is limited to type-2 diabetes / dysmetabolic populations.
compounds.verdict: Do not buy. Two decades and 200+ human studies later, the picture is dominated by poor oral bioavailability and inconsistent, often null clinical outcomes. Modest lipid/inflammatory shifts in type-2 diabetics do not generalise, and resveratrol has been shown to blunt exercise-training adaptations.
primary_sources: MDPI IJMS 2024, 25(2):747 (systematic review of resveratrol trials, gaps)
Lipid dose-response meta-analysis PMC9506025
Obesity metabolic meta-analysis, ScienceDirect S2667368124000433 (no significant clinical improvement)
Gliemann et al. 2013 J Physiol (blunts exercise adaptation)
Resveratrol bioavailability meta-analysis (rapid metabolism, low bioavailability)
